lessons.title: Traditional and modern farming

activities.prompt: How have farmers changed the way they grow food?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: Traditional farming methods
activities.body: Traditional farming treats the plant and soil as one complete system. The Indian seed drill prepared soil, planted seeds and closed the furrow together. Terrace farming cuts steps into hillsides to create flat farming land. Kulāgar is a traditional homestead where families grow many crops. Gokṛiṣhi is a farming system using cow manure for soil and bullocks for ploughing.
keyPoints: Traditional farming treats plants and soil as one system.
Terrace farming creates flat land on hillsides.
Kulāgar and Gokṛiṣhi are traditional farming systems.
activities.explanation: Traditional farming joins careful soil care with special farming methods.

activities.prompt: A farmer wants more output and healthy soil. Which farming approach fits best?
steps: The farmer wants modern productivity because farming output matters.
Traditional soil care matters because plants and soil work as one system.
Green Revolution methods can deplete groundwater and contaminate it with chemicals.
Sustainable farming fits best because it joins modern productivity with traditional wisdom.
activities.explanation: Think it through with Hooty.

activities.title: The seed drill's work
activities.prompt: What did the Indian seed drill do?
options: Prepared soil, planted seeds and closed the furrow
Cut steps into hillsides for flat farming land
Used cow manure for soil and bullocks for ploughing
Helped families grow many crops in a homestead
activities.explanation: The Indian seed drill prepared soil, planted seeds and closed the furrow together.

activities.title: One complete system
activities.prompt: Traditional farming treats the plant and soil as separate parts.
activities.explanation: Traditional farming treats the plant and soil as one complete system.

activities.title: Farming methods and features
activities.prompt: Match each farming method with its correct feature.
pairs: Prepared soil, planted seeds and closed the furrow
Cut steps into hillsides to create flat farming land
Traditional homestead where families grow many crops
Used cow manure for soil and bullocks for ploughing
activities.explanation: Each farming method has a different feature described in your book.

activities.title: Farming on a hillside
activities.prompt: Terrace farming cuts ______ into hillsides to create flat farming land.
activities.hint: These make flat farming land on a hillside.
activities.explanation: Cutting steps into hillsides creates flat farming land.

activities.title: Choosing sustainable farming
activities.prompt: What does sustainable farming combine?
options: Only chemicals and no traditional wisdom
Only old methods and no modern ideas
Modern productivity and traditional wisdom
Groundwater depletion and pesticide contamination
activities.explanation: Sustainable farming combines modern productivity with traditional wisdom.

activities.title: Natural pesticides
activities.prompt: Neem-based pesticides are natural and less harmful to the environment.
activities.explanation: Neem-based pesticides are natural and less harmful to the environment.

activities.title: The seed drill's order of work
activities.prompt: Put the Indian seed drill's actions in the correct order.
activities.explanation: The seed drill prepared the soil first, planted seeds next and closed the furrow last.

activities.prompt: A farmer uses one machine for sowing. What does this show about the Indian seed drill?
options: It only drops seeds into open soil.
It prepares soil, plants seeds and closes furrows.
It cuts flat steps into hillsides for farming.
It uses cow manure and bullocks for ploughing.

This is right because the drill does all three jobs together.
why.It cuts flat steps into hillsides for fa: This mistake confuses making land flat with planting seeds.
why.It uses cow manure and bullocks for plou: This mistake confuses cow manure and bullocks with seed sowing.

activities.explanation: This mistake thinks sowing leaves the furrow open.

activities.prompt: A source shows high-yield seeds and polluted water. Which change caused this?
options: Traditional farming, because it treats soil and plants together.
Terrace farming, because it makes flat land on hills.
The Green Revolution, because it introduced high-yielding seeds.
Organic farming, because it avoids chemical fertilisers.

why.Traditional farming, because it treats s: This mistake thinks traditional farming introduced high-yielding seed varieties.
why.Terrace farming, because it makes flat l: This mistake confuses flat hillside land with high-yielding seeds.
why.Organic farming, because it avoids chemi: This mistake thinks organic farming introduced the high-yielding seeds.

activities.explanation: This is right because it brought high-yielding seeds and chemical pollution.

lessons.title: Government support and farmers’ challenges

activities.prompt: How can government support help farmers, and what challenges must they overcome?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: How government support helps farmers
activities.body: Government support helps farmers. It gives access to seeds, fertilisers, pesticides and weather information. Irrigation uses water for farming, and cheaper electricity can reduce farming costs. Crop insurance schemes can offer money during hard times. Government buying of important crops helps farmers market their produce. Cold storages and digital information can help farmers obtain better prices. Small farms, extreme weather, water stress and debt create hard challenges.
keyPoints: Government support gives access to seeds, fertilisers, pesticides and weather information.
Cheaper electricity, crop insurance and crop buying support farmers.
Cold storages and digital information can help farmers obtain better prices.
activities.explanation: These supports can protect farmers and help them earn better.

activities.prompt: After untimely rain, a farmer needs help with money and costs. Which government support should the farmer use?
steps: Untimely rains increase crop-destruction risk, so losses may follow.
Crop insurance gives financial help because it supports farmers after crop losses.
Cheaper irrigation electricity reduces input costs because irrigation becomes less expensive.
Thus, insurance helps with losses, while cheaper power helps with running costs.
activities.explanation: Think it through with Hooty.

activities.title: Challenges faced by farmers
activities.body: Small farmers face challenges. It is hard for them to use tractors and other machines. Families may earn from livestock, poultry, beekeeping or fishing. Untimely rains and extreme weather can destroy crops. The Ganga is under stress because irrigation takes water and farming pumps out groundwater. Hard times can leave farmers trapped in debt after taking loans. Some estimates say that as many as 2,300 farmers every day abandon farming.
keyPoints: It is difficult for small farmers to use tractors and other machines.
Families may earn from livestock, poultry, beekeeping or fishing.
Poor weather, water stress and debt create serious challenges.
activities.explanation: These are serious challenges for farmers.

activities.prompt: Which support gives farmers access to farm inputs?
options: Lower power costs
Cold crop storage
Farm input access
Crop loss support
activities.explanation: Government support gives access to seeds, fertilisers, pesticides and weather information.

activities.prompt: Cheaper electricity for irrigation helps reduce input costs.
activities.explanation: Cheaper electricity for irrigation is meant to reduce input costs.

activities.prompt: Crop insurance schemes can give farmers ______ help.
activities.hint: This means help with money.
activities.explanation: Crop insurance schemes can give farmers financial help.

activities.prompt: Match each support with its result.
pairs: Access to seeds, fertilisers, pesticides and weather information
activities.explanation: Each support has the result shown in the lesson.

activities.prompt: Untimely rains can destroy crops. Which support can give farmers financial help?
options: Government crop buying
Cold storage support
Digital information aid
Crop insurance schemes
activities.explanation: Crop insurance schemes can give farmers financial help.

activities.prompt: Which activity can add to water pressure in farming areas?
options: Buying important crops
Pumping groundwater
Using cold storages
Reading weather information
activities.explanation: Irrigation takes water, and farming pumps out groundwater.

activities.prompt: Rain comes at the wrong time, and the crop is destroyed. Which support can help with money?
options: Crop insurance schemes can give financial help.
Cheaper irrigation electricity can give financial help.
Cold storages can give financial help after damage.
Government crop buying can give financial help.

why.Cheaper irrigation electricity can give: Cheaper electricity reduces input costs, not direct financial help.
why.Cold storages can give financial help af: Cold storage helps farmers get better prices, not financial help.
why.Government crop buying can give financia: Government buying creates a market, rather than giving financial help.

activities.explanation: Crop insurance gives money after losses caused by crop damage.

activities.prompt: A farmer has about three-fourths of a hectare. Before planting, the farmer needs seeds and rain information. What support helps, and what stays difficult?
options: Government support helps; using a tractor remains difficult.
Crop insurance helps; using a tractor becomes easy.
Cold storage helps; using a tractor becomes easy.
Government buying helps; using a tractor becomes easy.

why.Crop insurance helps; using a tractor be: Insurance gives financial help, not planting inputs or easier machinery.
why.Cold storage helps; using a tractor beco: Cold storage helps prices, not planting inputs or easier machinery.
why.Government buying helps; using a tractor: Crop buying helps marketing, not planting inputs or easier machinery.

activities.explanation: It provides seeds and weather information, while small holdings make tractors hard.

activities.prompt: A farmer gets cheaper electricity for irrigation. The farmer also takes a loan during hard times. What is likely?
options: Input costs may fall, but debt may remain.
Input costs and debt both surely disappear.
Input costs may rise, but debt may vanish.
Input costs may fall, and debt cannot affect farming.

why.Input costs and debt both surely disappe: Nothing says lower costs or loans make debt disappear.
why.Input costs may rise, but debt may vanis: Cheaper electricity reduces costs, while hard-time loans may leave debt.
why.Input costs may fall, and debt cannot af: Lower input costs do not remove the risk of debt.

activities.explanation: Cheaper electricity reduces input costs, but hard-time loans may leave debt.

activities.prompt: A farmer can use cold storage and digital price information. Another farmer's important crop is bought by the government. What can each gain?
options: First: better prices. Second: a market for produce.
First: financial help. Second: cheaper irrigation power.
First: access to seeds. Second: weather information.
First: less loan debt. Second: easier tractor use.

why.First: financial help. Second: cheaper i: Cold storage is for prices, and electricity supports irrigation, not crop buying.
why.First: access to seeds. Second: weather: Neither cold storage nor crop buying provides seeds or weather information.
why.First: less loan debt. Second: easier tr: The facts do not connect these supports to loan debt or tractors.

activities.explanation: Cold storage and digital information help prices, while buying creates a market.

activities.prompt: A map marks the Ganga as under stress. Which two farming actions can help explain this?
options: Taking river water for irrigation and pumping groundwater.
Buying crops and using cold storages for produce.
Getting weather information and buying crop insurance.
Using tractors and keeping poultry on farms.

why.Buying crops and using cold storages for: Buying crops and cold storage help marketing, not water stress.
why.Getting weather information and buying c: Weather information and insurance help with crop risks, not water use.
why.Using tractors and keeping poultry on fa: The stress is linked to water taking and pumping, not machinery or poultry.

activities.explanation: Irrigation takes river water, while farming pumps out groundwater.

activities.prompt: Some farming families earn from livestock, poultry, beekeeping or fishing. Yet as many as 2,300 farmers abandon farming each day. What does this suggest?
options: Farming offers different earnings, but some farmers still leave.
Farming gives every family enough earnings, so none leave.
All farming families earn only from one kind of work.
Farmer abandonment is lower than other kinds of work.

why.Farming gives every family enough earnin: The estimate shows some leaving, not that every family earns enough.
why.All farming families earn only from one: The fact gives several possible earnings, not only one.
why.Farmer abandonment is lower than other k: No fact compares farmer abandonment with other kinds of work.

activities.explanation: Families have several earnings, but the estimate still shows daily abandonment.

activities.context: Neha’s family earns its livelihood from agriculture and allied activities. Her mother grows crops, her father rears livestock, and their neighbour also rears fish. Neha learns that agri means field and culture means to cultivate. When discussing an old plain, they read about rice grains found in the Ganga Plain and ancient crops. Neha wonders how farming became important to people and how the work is shared today.
activities.prompt: Neha’s family wants to explain why the neighbour’s fish-rearing belongs to farming. What should they say?
options: It is an additional part of the farming work done by some farmers.
It is a form of forestry because it takes place outdoors.
It belongs only to animal husbandry and can never be part of farming.
It is an unrelated activity because agriculture is only crop growing.

why.It is a form of forestry because it take: Fish-rearing is not described as forestry.
why.It belongs only to animal husbandry and: Some farmers include fish-rearing in their farming work.
why.It is an unrelated activity because agri: Agriculture includes more than only growing crops.

activities.explanation: Some farmers rear fish as part of their farming.

activities.context: Neha’s family earns its livelihood from agriculture and allied activities. Her mother grows crops, her father rears livestock, and their neighbour also rears fish. Neha learns that agri means field and culture means to cultivate. When discussing an old plain, they read about rice grains found in the Ganga Plain and ancient crops. Neha wonders how farming became important to people and how the work is shared today.
activities.prompt: Neha notices her mother and other women doing agricultural work. Which statement best explains why their contribution is important?
options: Women account for at least three-quarters of those working in agriculture.
Men account for at least three-quarters of those working in agriculture.
Women account for only a small share of those working in agriculture.
Women and men make equal shares of those working in agriculture.

why.Men account for at least three-quarters: The fact states that at least 75 per cent are women.
why.Women account for only a small share of: A small share would contradict the stated proportion of women.
why.Women and men make equal shares of those: At least three-quarters being women does not support equal shares.

activities.explanation: At least 75 per cent of agriculture workers are women.

activities.prompt: Explain why agriculture is broader than only growing crops.
activities.answer: In its broad sense, agriculture covers farming, animal husbandry, forestry and horticulture. Farming itself includes preparing soil, growing plants and rearing livestock. Some farmers also rear fish as part of farming. Therefore, agriculture includes several kinds of work related to fields, plants, trees and animals.
points: Includes farming, animal husbandry, forestry and horticulture
Farming includes preparing soil and growing plants
Farming also includes rearing livestock
Some farmers rear fish as part of farming
activities.explanation: Compare your answer with the points a marker looks for.

activities.context: A farming family in northern India grows kharif crops and relies on southwest monsoon rain, which comes from June to September. A farming family in eastern India receives rain from the northeast monsoon, which prevails from October to December. On the Malabar and Coromandel plains, farming families receive rain from both monsoons. These examples show how India’s varied geography and climate influence the crops grown in different regions.
activities.prompt: If the southwest monsoon brings much less rain than usual in northern India, what should the farming family expect for its kharif crops?
options: The kharif crops could suffer because their crucial rain has been reduced.
The kharif crops would be safe because northeast monsoon rain would replace the missing rain.
The kharif crops would thrive because Zaid crops need southwest monsoon rain.
The kharif crops would not be affected because Rabi crops need monsoon rain.

why.The kharif crops would be safe because n: This wrongly assumes that northeast monsoon rain will reach and replace the missing rain.
why.The kharif crops would thrive because Za: This confuses kharif crops with Zaid, which is the summer-crop season.
why.The kharif crops would not be affected b: This confuses kharif crops with Rabi, which is the winter-crop season.

activities.explanation: Correct: Southwest monsoon rain is crucial for kharif crops in northern India.

activities.context: A farming family in northern India grows kharif crops and relies on southwest monsoon rain, which comes from June to September. A farming family in eastern India receives rain from the northeast monsoon, which prevails from October to December. On the Malabar and Coromandel plains, farming families receive rain from both monsoons. These examples show how India’s varied geography and climate influence the crops grown in different regions.
activities.prompt: If the southwest monsoon becomes weaker on the Malabar plain, but the northeast monsoon still brings rain, what can the farming family expect?
options: They will still receive northeast monsoon rain, but the overall rainfall may be lower.
They will receive no rain because the plains need both monsoons at the same time.
Their rainfall will remain exactly the same because a weaker southwest monsoon cannot affect the northeast monsoon.
They will receive only summer-season rain because Malabar plain crops belong to the Zaid season.

why.They will receive no rain because the pl: The two monsoons occur in different periods and do not have to occur at the same time.
why.Their rainfall will remain exactly the s: A weaker southwest monsoon can reduce the total rain even when the northeast monsoon continues.
why.They will receive only summer-season rai: Zaid names a cropping season for summer crops, not a monsoon or a source of rain.

activities.explanation: Correct: The northeast monsoon will still bring rain, although weaker southwest monsoon rain may reduce the total.

activities.prompt: Explain why different regions of India grow different crops.
activities.answer: India’s varied geography and climate influence the crops grown in different regions. The chapter identifies seven climate types and 15 agroclimatic zones, showing that conditions vary across India. Crop choices and cropping seasons therefore depend on the climate and monsoon rain available in each region.
points: India’s geography and climate influence regional crops.
The chapter introduces seven climate types.
India has 15 agroclimatic zones.
Regional conditions and monsoon rain affect crop choices.
activities.explanation: Compare your answer with the points a marker looks for.

activities.context: A farmer examines three plots. One contains dark, nutrient-rich humus mixed with soil. Another consists mostly of small grains of sand. The farmer learns that a third plot has laterite soil, which changes in hot weather as minerals are washed away. Knowing that soil type influences the crops grown, the farmer plans to match each crop to the plot’s soil.
activities.prompt: Which plan best follows what the farmer has learned?
options: Choose the same crop for all three plots because soil type does not affect crop growth.
Choose crops only by the colour of each plot’s soil.
Match different crops to each plot according to its soil type.
Choose a crop for the sandy plot and use it for all three plots.

why.Choose the same crop for all three plots: This contradicts the influence of soil type on crops.
why.Choose crops only by the colour of each: Colour alone does not identify the best crop for every plot.
why.Choose a crop for the sandy plot and use: This wrongly ignores how soil types influence crops.

activities.explanation: This correctly considers the different soil types.

activities.context: A farmer examines three plots. One contains dark, nutrient-rich humus mixed with soil. Another consists mostly of small grains of sand. The farmer learns that a third plot has laterite soil, which changes in hot weather as minerals are washed away. Knowing that soil type influences the crops grown, the farmer plans to match each crop to the plot’s soil.
activities.prompt: If the sandy plot were filled with soil formed from weathered volcanic rocks, what would be true?
options: It would become red soil because of its iron.
It would be black soil and would hold plenty of moisture.
It would become sandy soil with many small grains.
It would become laterite soil and harden in hot weather.

why.It would become red soil because of its: Red soil gets its colour from iron, not volcanic rock.
why.It would become sandy soil with many sma: Sandy soil consists mostly of small grains of sand.
why.It would become laterite soil and harden: Laterite soil hardens in hot weather as minerals are washed away.

activities.explanation: Black soil forms from weathered volcanic rocks and holds plenty of moisture.

activities.prompt: Explain how soil forms and how weathering helps in its formation.
activities.answer: Soil is the thin upper layer of Earth’s crust that supports plant life. It forms over millions of years as rocks break down and organic matter decays. Weathering breaks rocks and minerals into soil particles, helping create the soil that supports plants.
points: Soil is the thin upper layer of Earth’s crust.
It supports plant life.
Soil forms over millions of years.
Weathering breaks rocks and minerals into soil particles.
activities.explanation: Compare your answer with the points a marker looks for.

activities.context: In north-eastern India, a farmer farms terraced fields on a hill. Bamboo pipes carry spring water to the fields. The farmer ploughs along the hill slope’s curves and uses different crops in the same field during different seasons. The farmer also keeps seeds passed down through the family and gives some to relatives.
activities.prompt: Why are the farmer’s terraced fields and contour ploughing useful for protecting the soil?
options: Flat steps slow water runoff, while slope-following ploughing reduces soil erosion.
Flat steps provide crop water, while slope-following ploughing changes the seasonal crop.
Flat steps remove nutrients from the soil, while slope-following ploughing adds organic material.
Flat steps break down organic material, while slope-following ploughing passes seeds to families.

why.Flat steps provide crop water, while slo: Incorrect: terracing is not a water-supply method, and ploughing does not change crops.
why.Flat steps remove nutrients from the soi: Incorrect: terracing does not remove nutrients, and ploughing does not add organic material.
why.Flat steps break down organic material,: Incorrect: terracing does not break down organic material, and ploughing does not pass on seeds.

activities.explanation: Correct: terracing slows runoff, and contour ploughing reduces erosion.

activities.context: In north-eastern India, a farmer farms terraced fields on a hill. Bamboo pipes carry spring water to the fields. The farmer ploughs along the hill slope’s curves and uses different crops in the same field during different seasons. The farmer also keeps seeds passed down through the family and gives some to relatives.
activities.prompt: The farmer wants to follow crop rotation next season. What should the farmer change?
options: Plant a different crop in that field from one season to the next.
Plant several crops together in that field in every season.
Plant the same crop in that field in every season.
Plant one crop in that field, but move it to another field each season.

why.Plant several crops together in that fie: Incorrect: growing several crops together describes multiple cropping.
why.Plant the same crop in that field in eve: Incorrect: planting the same crop each season does not follow rotation.
why.Plant one crop in that field, but move i: Incorrect: rotation changes the crop, not the field in which it is grown.

activities.explanation: Correct: rotation involves changing crops in the same field between seasons.

activities.prompt: Explain the difference between crop rotation and multiple cropping.
activities.answer: Crop rotation changes the crop grown in the same field from one season to another. Multiple cropping grows several crops in the same field. Therefore, rotation is about changing crops between seasons, while multiple cropping is about growing more than one crop in the same field.
points: Crop rotation uses different crops in different seasons.
Multiple cropping grows several crops in the same field.
Rotation changes crops; multiple cropping increases the number of crops.
activities.explanation: Compare your answer with the points a marker looks for.

activities.context: A family living near a hillside farms on terraced land and grows many crops in its kulāgar. They use cow manure for the soil and bullocks for ploughing, as in Gokṛiṣhi. They also use an Indian seed drill and high-yielding seeds introduced during the Green Revolution. Recently, they noticed that groundwater around their farm was being depleted and contaminated by pesticides and fertilisers.
activities.prompt: What should the family do to follow sustainable farming after noticing contamination and groundwater depletion?
options: Adopt organic farming, avoid chemical fertilisers and pesticides, and use neem-based pesticides as a natural choice.
Continue using chemical fertilisers and pesticides because sustainable farming requires avoiding them.
Use neem-based pesticides but continue applying chemical fertilisers.
Choose only traditional methods and reject every modern farming practice.

why.Continue using chemical fertilisers and: This contradicts organic farming and the idea of sustainable farming.
why.Use neem-based pesticides but continue a: Using neem-based pesticides does not remove chemical fertilisers from the farming system.
why.Choose only traditional methods and reje: Sustainable farming combines modern productivity with traditional wisdom rather than rejecting modern methods.

activities.explanation: Organic farming avoids chemicals, while neem-based pesticides are natural and less harmful.

activities.context: A family living near a hillside farms on terraced land and grows many crops in its kulāgar. They use cow manure for the soil and bullocks for ploughing, as in Gokṛiṣhi. They also use an Indian seed drill and high-yielding seeds introduced during the Green Revolution. Recently, they noticed that groundwater around their farm was being depleted and contaminated by pesticides and fertilisers.
activities.prompt: If the family stopped cutting steps into the hillside, what important feature of terrace farming would they no longer have?
options: Flat farming land on the hillside.
A traditional homestead where the family can grow many crops.
A farming system that treats the plant and soil as one complete whole.
A machine that prepares soil, plants seeds and closes the furrow.

why.A traditional homestead where the family: Growing many crops describes the family’s kulāgar.
why.A farming system that treats the plant a: Treating the plant and soil as one system describes traditional farming.
why.A machine that prepares soil, plants see: The combined soil preparation, planting and furrow closing describes the seed drill.

activities.explanation: Terrace farming creates flat land by cutting steps into hillsides.

activities.prompt: Explain how traditional farming and sustainable farming are different.
activities.answer: Traditional farming treats the plant and the soil as one complete system. Sustainable farming does not reject modern methods; it combines modern productivity with traditional wisdom. It therefore seeks productive results while respecting the connection between plants and soil.
points: Traditional farming sees plants and soil as one system.
Sustainable farming combines modern and traditional ideas.
Traditional farming is not simply the opposite of modern farming.
activities.explanation: Compare your answer with the points a marker looks for.

activities.context: An average Indian farming family works about three-fourths of a hectare, so using a tractor or other machine is difficult. Untimely rains and extreme weather have put the crop at risk of destruction. The family may take a loan, which could leave it trapped in debt during hard times. It also earns from poultry. Government support, including crop insurance and cheaper irrigation electricity, may help, while cold storages and digital information may help it obtain better prices.
activities.prompt: Untimely rains have damaged the family’s crop. What should the family do to reduce the risk of being trapped in debt?
options: Use the government scheme that provides financial help when crops are damaged.
Use cheaper irrigation electricity as if it were payment for the crop loss.
Ask the government to buy the destroyed crop at a better price.
Rely on digital information and hope that it stops the crop from being destroyed.

why.Use cheaper irrigation electricity as if: Cheaper electricity reduces irrigation costs but does not provide crop-loss payment.
why.Ask the government to buy the destroyed: Government purchases concern important crops that can be marketed.
why.Rely on digital information and hope tha: Digital information may improve prices but cannot prevent destruction caused by extreme weather.

activities.explanation: Crop insurance can give financial help after crop damage.

activities.context: An average Indian farming family works about three-fourths of a hectare, so using a tractor or other machine is difficult. Untimely rains and extreme weather have put the crop at risk of destruction. The family may take a loan, which could leave it trapped in debt during hard times. It also earns from poultry. Government support, including crop insurance and cheaper irrigation electricity, may help, while cold storages and digital information may help it obtain better prices.
activities.prompt: Why is it difficult for this family to use a tractor on its plot?
options: The small size of the plot makes such machinery hard to use.
The family’s poultry earnings leave it no time to farm.
Cheaper irrigation electricity prevents the use of tractors.
Crop insurance pays for the machinery but covers only part of its cost.

why.The family’s poultry earnings leave it n: Poultry earnings are possible but are not the stated reason.
why.Cheaper irrigation electricity prevents: Cheaper electricity supports irrigation and does not prevent mechanisation.
why.Crop insurance pays for the machinery bu: Crop insurance gives financial help; it does not pay for tractors.

activities.explanation: Small farmers find it difficult to use tractors and other machines.

activities.prompt: How does government support help farming families?
activities.answer: Government support can lower costs by giving cheaper electricity for irrigation and access to seeds, fertilisers, pesticides and weather information. Crop insurance can provide financial help, while government purchases can help farmers market important crops. Cold storages and digital information may also help them obtain better prices.
points: Cheaper irrigation electricity reduces input costs.
Seeds, fertilisers, pesticides and weather information are available.
Crop insurance provides financial help.
Purchasing, cold storages and digital information support marketing and prices.
activities.explanation: Compare your answer with the points a marker looks for.

boss.title: Chapter challenge: The Story of Indian Farming

activities.prompt: Which group is included in the broad meaning of agriculture?
options: Farming, animal husbandry, forestry and horticulture
Farming, fishing, mining and poultry farming
Gardening, trading, weaving and pottery
Planting, forestry, mining and herding
activities.explanation: This wider meaning covers farming, animal husbandry, forestry and horticulture.

activities.prompt: Archaeologists found rice grains in the Ganga Plain in the 7th or 8th millennium BCE.
activities.explanation: Rice grains were found there during the 7th or 8th millennium BCE.

activities.prompt: Southwest monsoon rain is crucial for ______ crops in northern and central India.
activities.hint: This season is named for monsoon crops.
activities.explanation: Kharif crops need southwest monsoon rain in northern and central India.

activities.prompt: Which material is dark, organic matter that is rich in nutrients?
options: Humus
Alluvium
Weathering
Monsoon
activities.explanation: Humus is dark organic matter that is rich in nutrients.

activities.prompt: Put the Indian seed drill's jobs in order.
activities.explanation: The seed drill did all three jobs in this order.

activities.prompt: Afforestation means planting trees to help prevent soil erosion.
activities.explanation: The lesson defines afforestation as planting trees to prevent soil erosion.

activities.prompt: A hill farmer wants to slow water runoff. Which method is best?
options: Using crop rotation
Planting trees
Using terracing
Using drip irrigation
activities.explanation: Terracing creates flat farming steps on hills and slows water runoff.

activities.prompt: Rain-fed agriculture supplies crop water through artificial methods.
activities.explanation: Rain-fed agriculture depends entirely on rainfall. Artificial methods supply water in irrigated agriculture.

activities.prompt: Match each term with its description from the chapter.
pairs: Preparing soil, growing plants and rearing livestock
Brings rain from June to September
Treats the plant and soil as one complete system
Cuts steps into hillsides to create flat farming land
activities.explanation: Each pair connects a term with its description in the lesson.

chapters.title: India and Her Neighbours
chapters.summary: In this chapter: lesson 1: understanding india’s neighbourhood; lesson 2: india, china and pakistan; lesson 3: bangladesh and nepal; lesson 4: bhutan, myanmar and afghanistan.

lessons.title: Lesson 1: Understanding India’s Neighbourhood

activities.prompt: Which countries are India’s neighbours on land and across the sea?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: India’s Neighbourhood
activities.body: India has land-based neighbours and maritime neighbours. Land-based neighbours share a land boundary with India. Bangladesh and Myanmar lie to the east. A maritime neighbour is connected by a shared sea or ocean. Sri Lanka and the Maldives are immediate neighbours across the sea. Iran and Oman belong to India’s wider maritime neighbourhood. The ocean supports trade and cultural exchange. India’s ports help imports and exports.
keyPoints: Land-based neighbours share a land boundary.
Maritime neighbours share a sea or ocean.
India’s eastern neighbours include Bangladesh and Myanmar.
activities.explanation: This lesson shows how India connects with nearby and wider countries.

activities.prompt: Two maps show Nepal and the Maldives. Why are both India's neighbours?
steps: Nepal shares a land boundary, so it is a traditional neighbour.
The Maldives are connected by sea, so they are maritime neighbours.
India is both land-based and maritime, so both connections matter.
Therefore, Nepal and the Maldives are neighbours in different ways.
activities.explanation: Think it through with Hooty.

activities.title: India’s Maritime Connections
activities.body: The ocean has helped connect people through trade, cultural exchange and historical ties. Half of the world’s container ships travel through the Indian Ocean. India’s long coastline gives it a special maritime position. India’s ports serve as gateways for imports and exports. Regional cooperation helps bring peace, stability and shared progress.
keyPoints: The Indian Ocean carries many container ships.
India’s ports support imports and exports.
Regional cooperation supports peace and shared progress.
activities.explanation: These facts explain why India’s sea connections matter.

activities.title: Find a Land Neighbour
activities.prompt: Which country is a land-based neighbour of India?
options: Maldives
Pakistan
Sri Lanka
Singapore
activities.explanation: Good choice. Pakistan shares a land boundary with India.

activities.title: Neighbours in the East
activities.prompt: Bangladesh and Myanmar are India’s neighbours in the east.
activities.explanation: Yes. Both Bangladesh and Myanmar are neighbours in the east.

activities.title: India and the Sea
activities.prompt: India has always been a ______ nation as well as a land-based country.
activities.hint: This neighbour is connected through a shared sea or ocean.
activities.explanation: Well done. A maritime neighbour shares a sea or ocean with India.

activities.title: Meaning of Maritime Neighbour
activities.prompt: Which sentence describes a maritime neighbour?
options: It connects through a shared sea or ocean.
It connects through a shared land boundary.
It has no shared sea or ocean.
It connects only through shared land.
activities.explanation: A maritime neighbour is connected through a shared sea or ocean.

activities.title: Match India’s Neighbours
activities.prompt: Match each country with its place in India’s neighbourhood.
activities.explanation: Each country is matched using the kind of connection it has with India.

activities.title: India’s Maritime Position
activities.prompt: Which combination best describes India’s maritime position and role?
options: Long coastline and gateways for trade.
Short coastline and barriers for trade.
Land borders and gateways for inland travel.
Shared sea links and barriers for ocean travel.
activities.explanation: India’s long coastline gives it a special maritime position. Its ports support imports and exports.

activities.prompt: A shared border separates India and Nepal. What does this show?
options: They are land-based neighbours because they share a boundary.
They are maritime neighbours because a border crosses the sea.
They are not neighbours because borders always keep countries apart.
They are wider sea neighbours, but not immediate neighbours.

why.They are maritime neighbours because a b: This mistake confuses a sea connection with a land boundary.
why.They are not neighbours because borders: This mistake believes separation cancels shared land links.
why.They are wider sea neighbours, but not i: This mistake confuses wider maritime links with immediate neighbours.

activities.explanation: Right: a shared border proves they are land-based neighbours.

activities.prompt: Exports leave Indian ports for the Maldives and Oman. Which pair fits?
options: The Maldives are immediate; Oman is in the wider maritime neighbourhood.
The Maldives are wider; Oman is an immediate sea neighbour.
Both are immediate because exports can reach both of their ports.
Both are land-based because ships can carry exports to them.

why.The Maldives are wider; Oman is an immed: This mistake swaps the immediate and wider maritime groups.
why.Both are immediate because exports can r: This mistake assumes trade by sea proves a land boundary.
why.Both are land-based because ships can ca: This mistake calls sea connections land-based connections.

activities.explanation: Right: the Maldives are immediate sea neighbours, while Oman is wider.

activities.prompt: Bangladesh and Myanmar appear on India's eastern side. What does this show?
options: Both are eastern land-based neighbours of India.
Both are maritime neighbours connected only across the sea.
Both are western neighbours because maps can face differently.
Both lie outside India's neighbourhood because they are far away.

why.Both are maritime neighbours connected o: This mistake confuses eastern neighbours with maritime neighbours.
why.Both are western neighbours because maps: This mistake assumes maps can change a neighbour's direction.
why.Both lie outside India's neighbourhood b: This mistake treats distance as proof of no neighbourhood.

activities.explanation: Right: both countries belong to India's eastern neighbourhood.

activities.prompt: Half the world's container ships cross the Indian Ocean. What is shown?
options: The Indian Ocean is important to global container shipping.
The Indian Ocean carries only a small number of ships.
The Indian Ocean matters only to India's land neighbours.
The Indian Ocean has no link to container shipping.

why.The Indian Ocean carries only a small nu: This mistake reads half as only a small amount.
why.The Indian Ocean matters only to India's: This mistake limits the ocean's importance to land neighbours.
why.The Indian Ocean has no link to containe: This mistake denies any connection between the ocean and shipping.

activities.explanation: Right: half of all container ships shows the ocean's great shipping role.

activities.prompt: Two maritime neighbours face shared sea problems. Why should they cooperate?
options: Cooperation can bring peace, stability and shared progress.
Cooperation must bring conflict instead of shared progress.
Competition alone can create peace and stable progress.
Separation is safer because ports never need each other.

why.Cooperation must bring conflict instead: This mistake reverses cooperation's goal into conflict.
why.Competition alone can create peace and s: This mistake believes competition alone can create stability.
why.Separation is safer because ports never: This mistake assumes ports never need cooperation.

activities.explanation: Right: cooperation can bring peace, stability and shared progress.

lessons.title: Lesson 2: India, China and Pakistan

activities.prompt: What connects India, China, and Pakistan across mountains, history, and trade?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: India, China and Pakistan
activities.body: Strategic links mean connections between countries. India and China have shared links since 1950. The Himalayas separate India and China. Buddhism began in India. It reached China around the 1st century CE. Indian monks carried Buddhist teachings. Pakistan was once part of India. It was founded on religious grounds. The Kartarpur Corridor is a visa-free crossing for Indian pilgrims. Trade and dialogue are used to resolve border tensions.
keyPoints: India and China have shared strategic links since 1950.
The Himalayas separate India and China.
Pakistan was once part of India.
activities.explanation: The lesson shows links, differences and ways to handle tensions.

activities.prompt: A trader in China gets goods from India. China sends much more to India. What does this show?
steps: India sends goods to China, because these were its chief exports.
Trade is uneven by value, because China’s exports are worth much more.
China sells more to India than India sells to China.
activities.explanation: Think it through with Hooty.

activities.title: India’s Neighbour
activities.prompt: Which country is India’s largest neighbour?
options: Pakistan
China
India
Himalayas
activities.explanation: China is named as India’s largest neighbour.

activities.title: Monks and Buddhism
activities.prompt: Indian monks carried Buddhist teachings to China.
activities.explanation: Indian monks carried Buddhist teachings to China.

activities.title: Places and History
activities.prompt: Match each place with the correct history or relationship.
pairs: Founded on a religious basis, unlike India
Have had conflicts and a complex relationship
activities.explanation: Each pair joins a place with its history or relationship.

activities.title: When Links Began
activities.prompt: India and China have shared a strategic relationship since ____.
activities.hint: Choose the year when their relationship began.
activities.explanation: India and China have shared a strategic relationship since 1950.

activities.title: Comparing Exports
activities.prompt: Which statement about trade between India and China is correct?
options: China’s exports to India are worth more.
China’s exports to India are worth less.
Both countries’ exports are worth the same.
India’s exports to China are worth more.
activities.explanation: China’s exports to India are worth much more than India’s exports to China.

activities.title: Different Foundations
activities.prompt: Pakistan was founded on the same religious basis as India.
activities.explanation: Pakistan was founded on a religious basis, unlike India.

activities.title: Put Events in Order
activities.prompt: Put these events in the order they happened.
items: Buddhism reaches China around the 1st century CE
India and China share strategic links since 1950
activities.explanation: Buddhism began in India, reached China, and the countries shared links later.

activities.title: The Kartarpur Corridor
activities.prompt: Who can use the Kartarpur Corridor as a visa-free crossing?
options: Pakistani pilgrims
Indian pilgrims
Chinese pilgrims
Indian traders
activities.explanation: The Kartarpur Corridor is a visa-free crossing for Indian pilgrims.

activities.title: Handling Border Tensions
activities.prompt: Trade and dialogue are being used to resolve border tensions between India and China.
activities.explanation: Trade and dialogue are being used to resolve border disputes.

activities.prompt: China’s exports to India are worth much more than India’s exports. What does this show about trade?
options: China sells more by value to India than India sells to China.
India sells more by value to China than China sells to India.
Both countries sell the same total value to each other.
China buys more goods in total than India sells to China.

why.India sells more by value to China than: This reverses which country has more valuable exports.
why.Both countries sell the same total value: This assumes two-way trade means equal value.
why.China buys more goods in total than Indi: This confuses the number of goods with their value.

activities.explanation: China’s exports are worth more, so China sells more by value.

activities.prompt: Pakistan was once part of India. Which founding explanation fits the facts?
options: Pakistan was founded on a religious basis, unlike India.
Pakistan was founded on a trade basis, unlike India.
Both countries were founded on the same religious basis.
It was never later founded as a separate country.

why.Pakistan was founded on a trade basis, u: This swaps the religious basis for trade.
why.Both countries were founded on the same: This wrongly assumes both countries shared their founding basis.
why.It was never later founded as a separate: This confuses Pakistan’s earlier place in India with its founding.

activities.explanation: Pakistan had a religious basis, unlike India.

lessons.title: Lesson 3: Bangladesh and Nepal

activities.prompt: What connects Bangladesh and Nepal with India today?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: Bangladesh and Nepal
activities.body: India and Bangladesh share history, culture, language and river systems. A river system means connected rivers and their water flows. Bangladesh was born in 1971 after a war between India and Pakistan. It may face rising seas and stronger cyclones because of climate change. Nepal has a long, open border with India. Pilgrims cross it for sacred sites. The 1950 Treaty shapes their political relationship.
keyPoints: Shared culture and language connect India and Bangladesh.
Bangladesh was born in 1971 and may face climate risks.
Nepal shares a long, open border with India.
activities.explanation: These links show how culture, rivers and borders connect the countries.

activities.prompt: Two families, one in India and one in Bangladesh, use shared rivers for work. Why can the rivers support both families?
steps: Bangladesh and India share the Ganga and Brahmaputra river systems.
These rivers support farming, fishing and transport because people use them for work.
Shared rivers support livelihoods because this work helps people earn a living.
So the shared rivers can support both families' daily living.
activities.explanation: Think it through with Hooty.

activities.prompt: Nepal shares a long and ______ border with India.
activities.hint: Choose the word from the lesson.
activities.explanation: The lesson says Nepal shares a long and open border with India.

activities.prompt: India and Bangladesh share history, culture and language.
activities.explanation: These shared connections link India and Bangladesh.

activities.prompt: Which border of India is longer than its China border?
options: India's China border
Both borders
India's Bangladesh border
Neither border
activities.explanation: India's border with Bangladesh is longer than its border with China.

activities.prompt: Match each item with its correct detail.
activities.explanation: India and Bangladesh share river systems from the Ganga and Brahmaputra. These rivers support farming, fishing, transport and livelihoods.

activities.prompt: Which statement about India and Nepal is correct?
options: The 1950 Treaty shapes their relationship, and India is Nepal's largest trading partner.
India is Nepal's largest trading partner, but the 1950 Treaty shapes only trade.
The Treaty shapes their relationship, but India is Nepal's smallest trading partner.
India is Nepal's largest trading partner, and Nepal exports only garments to it.
activities.explanation: The 1950 Treaty shapes their political relationship. India is Nepal's largest trading partner. Nepal exports agricultural produce, handicrafts and garments to India.

activities.prompt: India and Bangladesh share history, culture and language. Bangla is spoken in Bangladesh and India's state of West Bengal. A child in West Bengal reads a Bangla book from Bangladesh. What does this show?
options: The same language helps connect people across both places.
Bangla is spoken in Bangladesh but not in West Bengal.
The two places cannot connect through shared language.
West Bengal is outside India because it speaks Bangla.

why.Bangla is spoken in Bangladesh but not i: This overlooks that Bangla is also spoken in West Bengal.
why.The two places cannot connect through sh: This confuses a shared language with a barrier to connection.
why.West Bengal is outside India because it: This wrongly thinks a shared language changes a place's location.

activities.explanation: Bangla is spoken in both places, so it helps connect people.

activities.prompt: A map uses the same scale for India's borders with Bangladesh and China. The Bangladesh border line is longer. A road follows each border. Which road covers more distance?
options: The road beside China's border is longer.
The road beside Bangladesh's border is longer.
Both roads cover exactly the same distance.
The map cannot compare the two roads.

why.The road beside China's border is longer: The fact says China's border is not the longer one.
why.Both roads cover exactly the same distan: A longer line on the same map scale means more distance.
The same scale lets the map compare both borders.

activities.explanation: India's border with Bangladesh is longer than its border with China.

activities.prompt: Nepal shares a long, open border with India. Pilgrims from both countries visit sacred sites across it. The 1950 Treaty of Peace and Friendship shapes their political relationship. The governments plan new border rules. What should guide their decision?
options: Check the treaty before changing how the countries relate.
Ignore the treaty because only pilgrims cross the border.
Use trade lists because they control political decisions.
Use pilgrim routes because they control political decisions.

why.Ignore the treaty because only pilgrims: This focuses on pilgrim travel and ignores the treaty's political role.
why.Use trade lists because they control pol: This confuses trading information with the treaty that guides politics.
why.Use pilgrim routes because they control: This confuses routes used by pilgrims with the treaty that guides politics.

activities.explanation: The treaty shapes India and Nepal's political relationship.

activities.prompt: India is Nepal's largest trading partner. Nepal exports agricultural produce, handicrafts and garments. A maker wants to sell these goods. Which country should the maker contact?
options: India, because only agricultural produce can be sold there.
India, because all three kinds of goods go there.
Bangladesh, because all three kinds of goods go there.
China, because all three kinds of goods go there.

why.India, because only agricultural produce: This leaves out handicrafts and garments, which Nepal also exports.
why.Bangladesh, because all three kinds of g: This confuses Bangladesh with India's role as Nepal's largest trading partner.
why.China, because all three kinds of goods: This confuses China with India's role as Nepal's largest trading partner.

activities.explanation: Nepal exports agricultural produce, handicrafts and garments to India.

lessons.title: Lesson 4: Bhutan, Myanmar and Afghanistan

activities.prompt: What makes Bhutan, Myanmar, and Afghanistan each special?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: Three Countries and Their Links with India
activities.body: Landlocked means no coastline. Bhutan is Drukyul, the Land of the Thunder Dragon. This small, landlocked Himalayan kingdom lies between India and China. Its rivers make hydroelectric power for India from flowing water. Bhutan measures progress through Gross National Happiness, which counts happiness. Myanmar borders Arunachal Pradesh, Nagaland, Manipur and Mizoram. India helped restore Ananda temple in Bagan. The Uttarāpatha route linked Ganga plains with Central Asia through Afghanistan.
keyPoints: Bhutan is Drukyul and lies between India and China.
Bhutan uses Gross National Happiness to measure progress.
Myanmar and Afghanistan have important links with India.
activities.explanation: This card introduces the main links between India and these countries.

activities.prompt: Families in Arunachal border areas now cross more easily. What explains this change?
steps: Arunachal Pradesh shares a border with Myanmar.
The 2018 agreement made movement easier in border areas.
Families can cross more easily because the agreement eased border movement.
So the change is explained by the 2018 Land Border Crossing Agreement.
activities.explanation: Think it through with Hooty.

activities.prompt: Which title is another name for Bhutan?
options: the Land of the Thunder Dragon
the Land of the Sacred Temple
the Land of the Ganga Plains
the Land of Central Asia
activities.explanation: Bhutan is also called Drukyul, or the Land of the Thunder Dragon.

activities.prompt: Bhutan is a small, landlocked Himalayan kingdom between India and China.
activities.explanation: Yes. Bhutan is small, landlocked and Himalayan. It lies between India and China.

activities.prompt: Arunachal Pradesh, Manipur, Mizoram and ______ all share a border with Myanmar.
activities.hint: This state is in India's northeast.
activities.explanation: Nagaland is one of the Indian states sharing a border with Myanmar.

activities.prompt: What does Bhutan use to measure national progress?
options: Gross National Happiness
Land Border Crossing Agreement
Ananda temple
Uttarāpatha trade route
activities.explanation: Bhutan uses Gross National Happiness to measure national progress.

activities.prompt: Why do Bhutanese pilgrims often visit India?
options: To see sacred Buddhist sites
To cross the Ananda temple
To reach Central Asia
To measure national happiness
activities.explanation: Bhutanese pilgrims frequently visit sacred Buddhist sites in India.

activities.prompt: Which set correctly matches each country with a link to India?
options: Bhutan—hydroelectric power; Myanmar—temple; Afghanistan—healthcare
Bhutan—pilgrimage; Myanmar—hydroelectric power; Afghanistan—agreement
Bhutan—agreement; Myanmar—healthcare; Afghanistan—hydroelectric power
Bhutan—happiness; Myanmar—agreement; Afghanistan—temple
activities.explanation: Only the first set is right. Bhutan's rivers help generate power for India, and India helped restore a temple in Myanmar. India also supports healthcare in Afghanistan.

activities.prompt: A map shows a small Himalayan country between India and China. It says Land of the Thunder Dragon. Which country is this?
options: Bhutan fits both the map and the dragon name.
Myanmar fits both the map and the dragon name.
Afghanistan fits both the map and the dragon name.
India fits both the map and the dragon name.

why.Myanmar fits both the map and the dragon: Myanmar has a long relationship with India, but not this dragon name.
why.Afghanistan fits both the map and the dr: Afghanistan is linked to the Uttarāpatha trade route, not Bhutan's dragon name.
why.India fits both the map and the dragon n: India lies beside Bhutan, but Bhutan is a separate kingdom.

activities.explanation: Bhutan is also called the Land of the Thunder Dragon.

activities.prompt: India helped restore the Ananda temple in Bagan. What wider connection does this show?
options: India and Myanmar have a relationship based on history, ethnicity and culture.
Bhutan and Myanmar have a relationship based on history, ethnicity and culture.
India and Afghanistan have a relationship based on history, ethnicity and culture.
India and Bhutan have a relationship based on history, ethnicity and culture.

why.Bhutan and Myanmar have a relationship b: This confuses Bhutan's links with India's links to Myanmar.
why.India and Afghanistan have a relationshi: This confuses Afghanistan's trade route with Myanmar's shared links.
why.India and Bhutan have a relationship bas: This confuses Bhutan's dragon name with Myanmar's shared links.

activities.explanation: It matches the long relationship based on history, ethnicity and culture.

lessons.title: Lesson 5: Sri Lanka and the Maldives

activities.prompt: What connects Sri Lanka, the Maldives, and India?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: Two Island Nations
activities.body: Sri Lanka is an island nation southeast of India, separated by the Palk Strait. They are about 32 km apart at their nearest point. Buddhism reached Sri Lanka in the 3rd century BCE. India and Sri Lanka cooperate culturally, economically and strategically. The Maldives has more than 1,100 small islands. India was among the first to recognise independent Maldives. Rising sea levels could submerge many islands.
keyPoints: Sri Lanka lies southeast of India, across the narrow Palk Strait.
They are only about 32 km apart at their nearest point.
The Maldives has more than 1,100 small islands and close ties with India.
activities.explanation: Notice their locations, history and links with India.

activities.prompt: A child asks why rising seas are a worry in the Maldives.
steps: The Maldives contains more than 1,100 small islands.
Because many islands could be submerged, many communities could face danger.
This is serious because one change can affect many island communities.
So rising sea levels could cause major changes in island life.
activities.explanation: Think it through with Hooty.

activities.title: The Narrow Sea
activities.prompt: Which narrow sea separates Sri Lanka from India?
options: Palk Strait
Wide Strait
Island Sea
Deep Sea
activities.explanation: The lesson calls the narrow sea between them the Palk Strait.

activities.title: Name the Strait
activities.prompt: The narrow sea between India and Sri Lanka is called the Palk ______.
activities.hint: Think of the narrow sea named in the lesson.
activities.explanation: The narrow sea separating the countries is the Palk Strait.

activities.title: Find the Direction
activities.prompt: Sri Lanka lies northwest of India.
activities.explanation: Sri Lanka is southeast of India, not northwest.

activities.title: Events in Time Order
activities.prompt: Put these events in time order, oldest first.
items: Buddhism introduced in the 3rd century BCE
Civil war begins in the mid-1980s
activities.explanation: This order starts with the oldest event and ends with the latest.

activities.title: Families During the War
activities.prompt: Where did many Tamil families go during Sri Lanka's war?
options: To the Maldives
To south India
To the Palk Strait
To Sri Lanka
activities.explanation: Many Tamil families moved from Sri Lanka to south India during the war.

activities.title: Links with the Maldives
activities.prompt: Which statement about India and the Maldives is fully correct?
options: The Palk Strait shaped their ties, and India gave quick help.
Mid-1980s conflict shaped their ties, and India gave quick help.
Centuries-old sea trade shaped their ties, and India gave quick help.
Rising sea levels shaped their ties, and India gave quick help.
activities.explanation: Sea trade shaped their old ties, and India gave quick help.

activities.prompt: Many Tamil families lived in Sri Lanka before the war. During the war, many left. The war lasted from the mid-1980s to around 2010. Where did many go, and why?
options: South India, because the war affected their family lives.
The Maldives, because they wanted to leave Sri Lanka's cities.
North India, because the war helped their family lives.
Sri Lanka's cities, because the war encouraged them to stay.

why.The Maldives, because they wanted to lea: This confuses the Maldives with south India.
why.North India, because the war helped thei: This wrongly treats the war as helping families.
why.Sri Lanka's cities, because the war enco: This assumes families chose to remain near the war.

activities.explanation: This is right: families moved to south India during the war.

activities.prompt: India and the Maldives have centuries-old ties shaped by maritime trade. Indian influences brought Tamil and Malayalam foods and arts to the Maldives. What does this show?
options: Long maritime ties helped Indian culture reach the Maldives.
Indian culture reached the Maldives only through recent wars.
Maritime trade kept Indian influences out of the Maldives.
Tamil and Malayalam cultures came from countries outside India.

why.Indian culture reached the Maldives only: This mistakes old trade ties for recent wars.
why.Maritime trade kept Indian influences ou: This assumes trade kept Indian influences out.
why.Tamil and Malayalam cultures came from c: This wrongly locates Tamil and Malayalam cultures outside India.

activities.explanation: This is right because maritime ties carried Indian foods and arts there.

activities.prompt: India and Sri Lanka combine cultural, economic and strategic cooperation. India was among the first to recognise independent Maldives. It also gave quick help during a tsunami and water crisis. What do these facts show about India's relations?
options: India's ties include cooperation, recognition, and practical help.
India recognised countries but refused practical help.
India helped only countries without cultural or strategic ties.
These facts show that all three countries share one government.

why.India recognised countries but refused p: This assumes recognition came without practical help.
why.India helped only countries without cult: This wrongly limits help to countries without existing ties.
why.These facts show that all three countrie: This confuses separate countries with one shared government.

activities.explanation: This is right because India showed cooperation, recognition, and practical help.

activities.prompt: The Maldives has more than 1,100 small islands. Rising sea levels could submerge many of them. What is a likely consequence for island life?
options: Many island communities could face major danger and change.
The islands would grow larger as the sea rises.
The islands would move north toward India.
The islands would lose their cultural and trading ties.

why.The islands would grow larger as the sea: This mistakes rising water for land that grows.
why.The islands would move north toward Indi: This wrongly imagines sea levels pulling islands north.
why.The islands would lose their cultural an: This confuses physical danger with weaker human ties.

activities.explanation: This is right because many islands could be submerged.

lessons.title: Lesson 6: Thailand, Malaysia, Singapore, Indonesia, Iran and Oman

activities.prompt: How are India and its neighbours connected through trade, travel, and shared history?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: Links Across Countries
activities.body: India has long links with Thailand, Malaysia, Singapore, Indonesia, Iran and Oman. Trade and cultural exchange with Thailand date back to ancient times. Indian workers from south India moved to Malaysia for rubber plantation work. Singapore's name means “lion city.” Indonesia is an archipelago, meaning a group of islands. India also works with Indonesia, Iran and Oman.
keyPoints: India and Thailand have had links since ancient times.
Workers from south India moved to Malaysia for plantation work.
India works with Indonesia, Iran and Oman.
activities.explanation: These links show how countries can work together.

activities.prompt: A student sees India helping with Iran's Chabahar Port. Why would these countries work together?
steps: India and Iran have shared close ties since the Bronze Age.
That long closeness helps explain why they can work together.
India is helping to develop Iran's Chabahar Port, showing cooperation in practice.
So the partnership builds on a relationship that is already very old.
activities.explanation: Think it through with Hooty.

activities.title: Working Together
activities.body: These links help countries work together in different ways. The India–Myanmar–Thailand Trilateral Highway improves trade and regional cooperation. India and Indonesia work together for peace, trade and sustainable development. India helps develop Iran's Chabahar Port. Oman shares a maritime boundary with India. This sea boundary has strategic importance.
keyPoints: The Highway improves trade and regional cooperation.
India and Indonesia work for peace and sustainable development.
Oman shares a maritime boundary with India.
activities.explanation: Cooperation can improve trade, peace and development.

activities.title: Ancient Links
activities.prompt: What has linked India and Thailand since ancient times?
options: Trade and cultural exchange
Military and sports ties
Modern trade alone now
School and sports links
activities.explanation: Thailand and India have had trade and cultural links since ancient times.

activities.title: Workers in Malaysia
activities.prompt: Indian workers from south India migrated to Malaysia to work on rubber plantations.
activities.explanation: Workers from south India moved to Malaysia to work on rubber plantations.

activities.title: Country Connections
activities.prompt: Match each country with its link from the lesson.
activities.explanation: Each country is linked to the feature stated in your book.

activities.title: A Port Project
activities.prompt: India is helping to develop Iran's ______ Port.
activities.hint: This port is in Iran.
activities.explanation: The lesson says India is helping to develop Chabahar Port in Iran.

activities.title: Oman's Sea Boundary
activities.prompt: What is said about Oman's maritime boundary with India?
options: It helps grow rubber.
It has strategic importance.
It began in ancient times.
It has no special importance.
activities.explanation: The lesson states that Oman's boundary with India has strategic importance.

activities.title: Find the Correct Row
activities.prompt: Which row links every country with a stated feature?
options: Thailand—old trade; Malaysia—rubber work; Indonesia—peace work; Oman—river border
Thailand—old trade; Singapore—rubber work; Indonesia—peace work; Iran—river border
Thailand—old trade; Malaysia—rubber work; Indonesia—many islands; Iran—port work
Thailand—rubber work; Malaysia—old trade; Indonesia—many islands; Oman—sea border
activities.explanation: The correct row matches the links for Thailand, Malaysia, Indonesia and Iran.

activities.prompt: An old book shows Indian goods and customs in Thailand. What does this suggest?
options: Their connection was already old in ancient times.
Thailand was once ruled as part of India.
India copied every custom found in Thailand.
Their connection began only in modern times.

why.Thailand was once ruled as part of India: This mistake turns cultural exchange into political rule.
why.India copied every custom found in Thail: This mistake turns exchange into exact copying.
why.Their connection began only in modern ti: This mistake treats an old link as a recent one.

activities.explanation: Ancient trade and cultural exchange connect India and Thailand.

activities.prompt: Travelers use the India–Myanmar–Thailand Highway. What is a likely result for the region?
options: Trade and regional cooperation can grow.
Travel between the three countries can become harder.
Local work can stop as goods travel faster.
The three countries can become less connected.

why.Travel between the three countries can b: This mistake thinks a shared road creates travel barriers.
why.Local work can stop as goods travel fast: This mistake assumes faster goods reduce all local work.
why.The three countries can become less conn: This mistake thinks a shared road makes countries less connected.

activities.explanation: The highway improves trade and regional cooperation.

activities.prompt: A map shows Indonesia as many large and small islands. What can we conclude about its shape?
options: Indonesia is an archipelago with several large islands.
Indonesia is one island with many small lakes.
Indonesia is many countries joined by narrow seas.
Indonesia is one island with many small hills.

why.Indonesia is one island with many small: This mistake mistakes separate islands for lakes.
why.Indonesia is many countries joined by na: This mistake mistakes one country's islands for separate countries.
why.Indonesia is one island with many small: This mistake mistakes separate islands for hills on one island.

activities.explanation: Indonesia is an archipelago with several large and many smaller islands.

activities.prompt: A worker from south India moves to Malaysia for a job. What work explains the move?
options: To work on Malaysia's rubber plantations.
To build the highway between three countries.
To run a trading company in Singapore.
To teach plantation work in south India.

why.To build the highway between three count: This mistake connects the move with highway building.
This mistake connects the move with trading work in Singapore.
This mistake turns the worker into a teacher in India.

activities.explanation: Workers from south India moved to Malaysia for rubber plantation work.

activities.prompt: A map shows Oman sharing India's sea boundary. Why might India pay attention to Oman?
options: Oman's position can have strategic importance.
Oman must share every land border with India.
Oman's position makes sea links unnecessary.
Oman's position matters only for rubber work.

why.Oman must share every land border with I: This mistake mixes a sea boundary with every land border.
why.Oman's position makes sea links unnecess: This mistake thinks shared sea borders remove the need for links.
why.Oman's position matters only for rubber: This mistake connects Oman with Malaysia's rubber plantations.

activities.explanation: Oman has a maritime boundary with India and has strategic importance.
