activities.context: A remote village sends goods made there to a market along a road. Farmers irrigate their fields with water from a canal and with electric water pumps. A nearby solar park supplies electricity, while telephone lines and the internet help residents communicate with nearby cities. Now the road cannot be used. The village plans to repair it and hopes to add a bridge so that transport links to the market improve.
activities.prompt: If the road is repaired, what is the most likely next result?
options: Goods can reach the market again, so trade may grow.
Farmers may find less need to irrigate because goods can travel more easily.
People may rely less on telephone lines and the internet because transport is easier.
The solar park may be used to carry goods now that the road works.

why.Farmers may find less need to irrigate b: Easier transport does not remove the need to irrigate fields.
why.People may rely less on telephone lines: Communication remains useful even when transport improves.
why.The solar park may be used to carry good: A solar park supplies electricity; it is not a transport route.

activities.explanation: The road connects goods with a market.

activities.context: A remote village sends goods made there to a market along a road. Farmers irrigate their fields with water from a canal and with electric water pumps. A nearby solar park supplies electricity, while telephone lines and the internet help residents communicate with nearby cities. Now the road cannot be used. The village plans to repair it and hopes to add a bridge so that transport links to the market improve.
activities.prompt: If the solar park cannot supply electricity, what is the most likely effect on farming?
options: Some farmers may find it harder to irrigate because electric water pumps cannot run.
Farmers will be unable to use canal water for irrigation.
The road will stop carrying goods to the market.
Telephone and internet connections will begin carrying goods physically.

why.Farmers will be unable to use canal wate: Canal water can still be used for irrigation.
why.The road will stop carrying goods to the: A road transports goods independently of the solar park's electricity supply.
why.Telephone and internet connections will: Communication networks do not physically carry goods.

activities.explanation: Electric pumps need electricity to run.

activities.prompt: Why does physical infrastructure play an important role in everyday life?
activities.answer: Physical infrastructure forms a vast network of roads, bridges, railways, utilities and communication systems. These connect places, supply water and electricity, and help people communicate. They make life easier, support trade and tourism, reach remote areas and help farmers irrigate their fields.
points: Connects cities and villages
Supports trade and tourism
Reaches remote areas
Supports farming and daily needs
activities.explanation: Compare your answer with the points a marker looks for.

activities.context: A family travelling between Assam and Arunachal Pradesh found that the Dhola Sadiya Bridge across the Lohit River allowed year-round travel and reduced their travel time. In another area of difficult terrain, where a highway could not be built, travellers could use a living root bridge. The Khāsi and Jaintia tribes craft such bridges using tree roots. Meanwhile, a farmer relied on local roads to carry vegetables and fruits to the market before they spoil.
activities.prompt: If the river becomes difficult to cross at some time of the year, what can the family still expect because of this bridge?
options: They can continue crossing without waiting for another season.
They must wait until the river becomes easier to cross.
They must use an expressway instead.
They will take longer to complete the trip.

why.They must wait until the river becomes e: This contradicts the bridge’s year-round travel facility.
An expressway does not provide a crossing of this river.
why.They will take longer to complete the tr: The bridge has reduced travel time.

activities.explanation: The bridge allows travel throughout the year.

activities.context: A family travelling between Assam and Arunachal Pradesh found that the Dhola Sadiya Bridge across the Lohit River allowed year-round travel and reduced their travel time. In another area of difficult terrain, where a highway could not be built, travellers could use a living root bridge. The Khāsi and Jaintia tribes craft such bridges using tree roots. Meanwhile, a farmer relied on local roads to carry vegetables and fruits to the market before they spoil.
activities.prompt: If the farmer cannot carry vegetables and fruits to the market promptly, what is likely to happen?
options: They may spoil before being sold.
They will travel farther but remain fresh.
They will be kept longer and stay fresh.
They will reach markets without being damaged.

why.They will travel farther but remain fres: A longer journey does not prevent spoiling.
Keeping them longer would not keep them fresh.
why.They will reach markets without being da: They may be damaged if they do not reach the market promptly.

activities.explanation: Prompt delivery helps prevent vegetables and fruits from spoiling.

activities.prompt: Explain the difference between local roads and expressways.
activities.answer: Local roads help children reach school, farmers carry crops, and ambulances reach hospitals. Expressways are fast roads that connect cities across different states. Thus, local roads help with local travel and services, while expressways help people travel quickly between cities in different states.
points: Local roads help children reach school.
Local roads help farmers and ambulances.
Expressways are fast roads.
Expressways connect cities across states.
activities.explanation: Compare your answer with the points a marker looks for.

activities.context: A clothing and electronics firm wants to supply customers in another part of India. It can send its cargo by train, while rail expansion links the firm to new markets where settlements are growing. Residents can also choose metro trains in 23 Indian cities to reduce road traffic and shorten travel times. Indian Railways carries more than 20 million passengers every day and provides about 1.21 million direct jobs.
activities.prompt: If many residents in the city shifted their journeys from roads to metro trains, what would be the likely result?
options: Road traffic would decrease, and many journeys could take less time.
Road traffic would increase, and most journeys would take longer.
Road traffic would decrease, but every journey would take longer.
Road traffic would remain the same, but most metro journeys would take longer.

why.Road traffic would increase, and most jo: This reverses both likely effects of increased metro use.
why.Road traffic would decrease, but every j: Less traffic is possible, but longer journey times are not a likely combined result.
why.Road traffic would remain the same, but: Metro use can change traffic levels, and it can shorten rather than lengthen travel times.

activities.explanation: Metro trains can reduce road traffic and shorten travel times.

activities.context: A clothing and electronics firm wants to supply customers in another part of India. It can send its cargo by train, while rail expansion links the firm to new markets where settlements are growing. Residents can also choose metro trains in 23 Indian cities to reduce road traffic and shorten travel times. Indian Railways carries more than 20 million passengers every day and provides about 1.21 million direct jobs.
activities.prompt: Why might extending a railway into an area encourage businesses and settlements to grow there?
options: The railway helps people and goods reach more places, allowing businesses to sell to buyers farther away.
The railway mainly carries troops, so ordinary goods cannot support local trade.
The railway makes nearby markets harder to reach, so buyers and sellers avoid the area.
Only passenger numbers matter, so extending the line cannot encourage trade or settlements.

why.The railway mainly carries troops, so or: Cargo trains carry goods, so railways can also support businesses.
why.The railway makes nearby markets harder: Railway expansion has helped markets and settlements grow.
why.Only passenger numbers matter, so extend: Railways affect trade and settlements, not only passenger numbers.

activities.explanation: Better rail links support the movement of people and goods and help trade expand.

activities.context: A clothing and electronics firm wants to supply customers in another part of India. It can send its cargo by train, while rail expansion links the firm to new markets where settlements are growing. Residents can also choose metro trains in 23 Indian cities to reduce road traffic and shorten travel times. Indian Railways carries more than 20 million passengers every day and provides about 1.21 million direct jobs.
activities.prompt: If the firm sends its textiles and electronics by cargo train, what benefit could follow?
options: It can reach customers beyond its present area, helping trade expand.
It would have to abandon textiles and electronics because cargo trains carry only coal and grains.
It would gain no market benefit because cargo trains do not move goods.
It would need to send all its goods by metro because cargo trains cannot travel beyond one city.

why.It would have to abandon textiles and el: Cargo trains carry products such as textiles and electronics as well as coal and grains.
why.It would gain no market benefit because: Cargo trains move goods, so their use can benefit trade.
why.It would need to send all its goods by m: Metro trains serve cities, while cargo trains can carry the firm's goods over the railway network.

activities.explanation: Cargo trains carry textiles and electronics and can help firms supply customers farther away.

activities.prompt: Explain why railways were important to the British in controlling India and to Indian trade and growth.
activities.answer: Railways changed India in two connected ways. They moved goods across the country, supporting trade and the growth of markets and settlements. They also moved troops more quickly, which helped the British control India more tightly. Therefore, railways served economic and political purposes.
points: Railways helped goods move across India.
Their expansion encouraged trade.
New markets and settlements could grow.
They moved troops quicker and tightened British control.
activities.explanation: Compare your answer with the points a marker looks for.

activities.context: After a flood, relief workers must send aid to people in a mountainous area. The workers need to deliver relief supplies quickly to a place that is difficult to reach. A business also has perishable goods ready for shipment. The relief team and the business compare their needs before choosing transport, while planners review how Indian airports and ports support movement across the country and overseas.
activities.prompt: What transport should the relief team choose for delivering aid to the mountainous area?
options: A cargo flight, because it can carry the aid and reach the mountainous area quickly.
A passenger flight, because passenger flights are the best way to move relief supplies.
A cargo ship, because ships are the fastest way to reach difficult places.
A ship, because lower cost matters more than speed in an emergency.

why.A passenger flight, because passenger fl: Incorrect: passenger flights mainly carry people.
why.A cargo ship, because ships are the fast: Incorrect: ships are not the fastest option for difficult areas.
why.A ship, because lower cost matters more: Incorrect: cheap transport does not meet the urgent need for speed.

activities.explanation: Correct: cargo flights can deliver aid and reach difficult places quickly.

activities.context: After a flood, relief workers must send aid to people in a mountainous area. The workers need to deliver relief supplies quickly to a place that is difficult to reach. A business also has perishable goods ready for shipment. The relief team and the business compare their needs before choosing transport, while planners review how Indian airports and ports support movement across the country and overseas.
activities.prompt: The business now has heavy goods for a long-distance trade and wants to reduce transport cost. What should it use?
options: A cargo ship, because ships carry heavy goods cheaply over long distances.
A cargo flight, because air transport is always the cheapest method.
A passenger flight, because passenger flights move goods at no cost.
A cargo ship, because ships reach mountains, deserts and forests more easily than aircraft.

why.A cargo flight, because air transport is: Incorrect: air transport is fast, but not always cheapest.
why.A passenger flight, because passenger fl: Incorrect: passenger flights carry people rather than trade goods.
why.A cargo ship, because ships reach mounta: Incorrect: aircraft can easily reach difficult places.

activities.explanation: Correct: ships are cheaper for heavy, long-distance transport.

activities.prompt: Explain why air transport is more suitable than shipping for delivering disaster aid to a mountainous area.
activities.answer: Air transport is the fastest way to connect people and places, and aircraft can easily reach difficult places such as mountains. Flights can deliver aid during floods and earthquakes. Shipping is cheaper for heavy goods over long distances, but speed and difficult access matter most for urgent disaster aid.
points: Air transport is the fastest.
Aircraft can reach mountains easily.
Flights can deliver aid during disasters.
Ships are cheaper for heavy, long-distance transport.
activities.explanation: Compare your answer with the points a marker looks for.

activities.context: When Rani’s mobile tower loses electricity, she cannot send the voice note she wants to share with her friend. Once electricity returns, her voice note travels from the mobile tower through fibre cables buried under fields and roads. It then passes through satellites and servers before reaching the other phone. Students in remote areas can use online classes, digital libraries and educational videos when communication infrastructure works.
activities.prompt: What is likely to happen after electricity returns to Rani’s mobile tower?
options: Her voice note can begin travelling through the communication network.
Her voice note will reach the other phone without using any network.
Her voice note will wait until her friend attends an online class.
Her voice note will reach the other phone before passing through fibre cables.

why.Her voice note will reach the other phon: Electricity allows the transmission process to continue.
why.Her voice note will wait until her frien: The message follows the route through cables, satellites and servers.
why.Her voice note will reach the other phon: It does not need to wait for an online class.

activities.explanation: The tower needs electricity to receive Rani’s voice note.

activities.context: When Rani’s mobile tower loses electricity, she cannot send the voice note she wants to share with her friend. Once electricity returns, her voice note travels from the mobile tower through fibre cables buried under fields and roads. It then passes through satellites and servers before reaching the other phone. Students in remote areas can use online classes, digital libraries and educational videos when communication infrastructure works.
activities.prompt: Rani’s friend is in a remote area and the communication infrastructure is working. Which activities can the friend use?
options: Join an online lesson and use a digital library.
Sell products worldwide and receive mobile alerts.
Apply for government documents and make complaints.
Send voice notes only during natural disasters.

why.Sell products worldwide and receive mobi: E-commerce and e-governance are different uses of communication infrastructure.
why.Apply for government documents and make: Mobile alerts help people respond during natural disasters.
why.Send voice notes only during natural dis: Voice notes are not limited to disasters.

activities.explanation: Remote students can use online classes and digital libraries.

activities.context: In one community, damage to public infrastructure made life harder for everyone. The panchayat and municipal services began planning better waste, sewer and traffic management. Residents also asked for cleaner energy, environment-friendly materials and facilities that met the needs of children, elderly people and disabled persons. Kautilya’s Arthaśhāstra described state, village and sabhās support in building and maintaining roads and waterways.
activities.prompt: Why did Kautilya recommend punishments and fines for people who damaged infrastructure?
options: To discourage people from damaging shared infrastructure
To give priority only to private transport
To remove the community's shared responsibility
To narrow roads according to expected traffic

why.To give priority only to private transpo: Fines are meant to protect shared assets, not favour private transport.
why.To remove the community's shared respons: Punishment does not remove the community's shared duty to maintain infrastructure.
why.To narrow roads according to expected tr: Road widths should reflect expected traffic, not serve as the purpose of fines.

activities.explanation: Fines discourage damage and protect shared facilities.

activities.context: In one community, damage to public infrastructure made life harder for everyone. The panchayat and municipal services began planning better waste, sewer and traffic management. Residents also asked for cleaner energy, environment-friendly materials and facilities that met the needs of children, elderly people and disabled persons. Kautilya’s Arthaśhāstra described state, village and sabhās support in building and maintaining roads and waterways.
activities.prompt: Which result is most likely if the new infrastructure does not meet the needs of children, elderly people and disabled persons?
options: Some people may not be able to use the facilities properly
Everyone will use the facilities equally well
Only children’s access will be affected
The facilities will automatically meet every group’s needs

why.Everyone will use the facilities equally: Equal access cannot be assumed if some groups’ needs are ignored.
why.Only children’s access will be affected: Children are not the only group whose needs must be considered.
why.The facilities will automatically meet e: New facilities do not automatically meet every group’s needs.

activities.explanation: Facilities that ignore accessibility needs cannot properly serve all groups.

activities.prompt: Explain why damage to public infrastructure affects the whole community.
activities.answer: Damage to public infrastructure makes life harder for everyone because shared facilities serve the whole community. When infrastructure is damaged, people’s everyday needs become harder to meet. This is why everyone must share responsibility for caring for public infrastructure, rather than leaving the work to only one person or group.
points: Public infrastructure serves the whole community.
Damage makes life harder for everyone.
Care of infrastructure requires shared responsibility.
Responsibility should not rest with only one group.
activities.explanation: Compare your answer with the points a marker looks for.

chapters.title: Banks and the Magic of Finance
chapters.summary: In this chapter: financial infrastructure and the role of banks; bank accounts, savings and compounding; loans, banking access and the rbi; payment modes and systems.

lessons.title: Financial Infrastructure and the Role of Banks

activities.prompt: How do banks help people and communities manage money and build futures?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: How Banks Support Money and Infrastructure
activities.body: Financial infrastructure is a connected group of banks, payment systems and stock markets. It helps people, businesses and the government manage money and make financial transactions. It makes funding for infrastructure development and maintenance possible. Roads, railways and telecommunication are examples of physical infrastructure. A deposit is money a person gives to a bank. A loan is money a bank gives to a borrower for specific purposes.
keyPoints: Financial infrastructure includes banks, payment systems and stock markets.
It helps manage money and supports infrastructure funding.
Banks collect deposits and give loans for specific purposes.
activities.explanation: Banks are an important part of the network that helps everyone manage money.

activities.prompt: Rima needs more money for her bamboo business, but she only has some.
steps: Rima needs money for her bamboo business.
She has some money, but she still needs the remaining amount.
The bank gives that remaining amount as a loan.
This solves her problem because the loan has a specific business purpose.
activities.explanation: Think it through with Hooty.

activities.title: Choose the Financial Network
activities.prompt: Which group belongs to financial infrastructure?
options: banks, factories and large railway stations
banks, payment systems and stock markets
roads, forests and mountain tourism centres
banks, schools and large railway stations
activities.explanation: Financial infrastructure includes banks, payment systems and stock markets.

activities.title: Money Given to a Bank
activities.prompt: A bank collects money from people as deposits.
activities.explanation: Deposits are money people give to a bank.

activities.title: Money Lent by Banks
activities.prompt: A bank gives money to borrowers as a ______.
activities.hint: Borrowers receive it for specific purposes.
activities.explanation: The money given to a borrower is called a loan.

activities.title: Match the Parts
activities.prompt: Match each item with its correct example or meaning.
pairs: banks, payment systems and stock markets
activities.explanation: Each pair connects an idea with its correct example or meaning.

activities.title: Rima's Business Loan
activities.prompt: What does the bank provide for Rima's bamboo business?
options: the remaining amount as a loan
the whole amount as a deposit
a payment system for bamboo
stock market shares for bamboo
activities.explanation: The bank provides the remaining amount Rima needs as a loan.

activities.title: Funding Infrastructure
activities.prompt: Why does financial infrastructure help roads, railways and telecommunication?
options: It replaces their roads and telecommunication.
It collects deposits from their workers.
It funds their development and maintenance.
It turns them into banks and markets.
activities.explanation: Financial infrastructure makes funding for development and maintenance possible.

activities.prompt: Navdeep has surplus money. Rima needs money for her bamboo business. What can the bank do?
options: Use deposits to give Rima a business loan.
Give Rima a loan for no specific purpose.
Keep both amounts because banks never make loans.
Give Navdeep’s money to Rima without any loan.

why.Give Rima a loan for no specific purpose: This misses the rule that loans have specific purposes.
why.Keep both amounts because banks never ma: This wrongly thinks banks only collect deposits.
why.Give Navdeep’s money to Rima without any: This wrongly treats a loan as a simple money transfer.

activities.explanation: This uses deposits to make a loan for a specific purpose.

activities.prompt: Rima has some money for her bamboo business. What changes if the bank lends the remaining amount?
options: She can finish funding her bamboo business.
She must still find all business money elsewhere.
Her business must wait because loans have no purpose.
She can use the loan for any business purpose.

why.She must still find all business money e: This wrongly assumes the bank’s loan does not help her.
why.Her business must wait because loans hav: This wrongly believes loans do not have specific purposes.
why.She can use the loan for any business pu: This ignores that Rima’s loan is for her bamboo business.

activities.explanation: The loan supplies the remaining money she needs.

activities.prompt: A map shows banks connected to people, businesses and government. Its arrows show deposits and loans. What does this map show?
options: How money moves through financial infrastructure.
Where roads and railways are placed.
Where telecommunication towers are placed.
Where stock markets are placed.

This confuses financial infrastructure with physical infrastructure.
why.Where telecommunication towers are place: This confuses telecommunication with financial infrastructure.
This focuses on one part instead of the whole network.

activities.explanation: The map shows money moving through a financial network.

activities.prompt: Navdeep has extra money. Why does he put his surplus money in a bank?
options: His deposit can help fund borrowers’ specific purposes.
His deposit can build roads and railways directly.
His deposit becomes his own loan from the bank.
His deposit removes the need for other financial services.

why.His deposit can build roads and railways: This confuses financial and physical infrastructure.
why.His deposit becomes his own loan from th: This reverses the roles of depositors and borrowers.
why.His deposit removes the need for other f: This wrongly suggests one deposit replaces the whole system.

activities.explanation: Banks collect deposits and make loans for specific purposes.

activities.prompt: A borrower wants a loan to repair a shop. The bank agrees to give the loan. How should the borrower use it?
options: Only for the shop repair.
For any purpose the borrower chooses.
Only for buying food and paying bills.
Only for paying another bank’s deposit.

This ignores the loan’s stated purpose.
This mistakes daily spending for the shop repair.
This confuses a deposit with a loan’s purpose.

activities.explanation: This follows the rule that loans have specific purposes.

lessons.title: Bank Accounts, Savings and Compounding

activities.prompt: Could your savings grow while you wait, and how would that happen?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: Bank Accounts and Their Uses
activities.body: Opening a bank account lets you use services like saving, withdrawing and borrowing. Farmers, shopkeepers, nurses, businesses and institutions use these services. A savings account is mainly for individuals. A current account helps businesses and traders make and receive payments. A fixed deposit account keeps money for a fixed period. Banks keep deposits safe and lend them to businesses or other people.
keyPoints: You must open a bank account before using bank services.
Different accounts help people and businesses.
Banks keep deposits safe and lend them.
activities.explanation: These services connect everyday life with saving, payments, borrowing and keeping money safe.

activities.prompt: A shopkeeper wants to receive payments and make business payments. Which bank account should they open?
steps: The shopkeeper needs a current account because it helps businesses make and receive payments.
A shopkeeper must first open a bank account because this is needed to use bank services.
Therefore, the shopkeeper should open a current account for business payments.
activities.explanation: Think it through with Hooty.

activities.title: Interest, Compounding and Passbooks
activities.body: Depositing money in a bank helps keep it safe. The bank also lends deposits to businesses or other people. People who deposit money receive extra money over a regular period as interest. Compounding happens when interest is earned on previous interest. A passbook records all receipts and payment transactions in an account.
keyPoints: Interest is extra money paid to depositors.
Compounding means earning interest on earlier interest.
A passbook records account transactions.
activities.explanation: Interest can grow further when it earns interest of its own.

activities.prompt: What must a person or business do before using bank services?
options: Open a bank account
Start saving
Start withdrawing
Start borrowing
activities.explanation: A person or business must open an account before using bank services.

activities.prompt: A savings account is mainly for businesses.
activities.explanation: A savings account is mainly for individuals.

activities.prompt: Match each account with its main purpose.
pairs: Helps traders make and receive payments
Keeps money for a fixed period
activities.explanation: Each account has a main purpose described in the lesson.

activities.prompt: Which situation shows compounding?
options: Earning interest on previous interest
Keeping money for a fixed period
Recording receipts and payment transactions
Helping a trader receive payments
activities.explanation: Compounding happens when earlier interest earns more interest.

activities.prompt: Compounding happens when interest is earned on ______ interest.
activities.hint: Think about interest earned earlier.
activities.explanation: Compounding means interest is earned on interest from earlier.

activities.prompt: Put these steps in order.
items: Keep a deposit at the bank
activities.explanation: An account comes first, followed by a deposit, interest and compounding.

activities.prompt: A shopkeeper must make payments and receive payments. Which account fits best?
options: A savings account, mainly for individuals.
A current account for business payments.
A fixed deposit for a fixed period.
A savings account for business payments.

why.A savings account, mainly for individual: This uses a savings account although it is mainly for individuals.
This confuses keeping money for a fixed period with making business payments.
This wrongly treats a savings account as best for business payments.

activities.explanation: This is right because a current account helps businesses make and receive payments.

activities.prompt: A trader needs regular payments. A person wants money kept for a fixed period. Which pairing fits?
options: A current account; a fixed deposit account.
A savings account; a current account.
A fixed deposit account; a savings account.
A current account; a savings account.

This swaps the account purposes and confuses payments with keeping money fixed.
why.A fixed deposit account; a savings accou: This reverses the pairing and treats fixed savings as business payments.
This treats current accounts as fixed-term and savings accounts as business-payment accounts.

activities.explanation: This is right because current accounts help with payments while fixed deposits keep money for a fixed period.

activities.prompt: Interest is added to a deposit. Then new interest is earned on earlier interest. What causes the total to grow?
options: Previous interest also earns interest.
Only the original deposit earns interest.
The bank returns the deposit unchanged.
The account receives no extra money.

why.Only the original deposit earns interest: This wrongly assumes that the original deposit is the only thing earning interest.
This mistakes interest growth for a deposit that stays unchanged.
This confuses earning interest with receiving no extra money.

activities.explanation: This is right because interest earned on earlier interest makes the total grow.

activities.prompt: The example shows a total of ₹1,123.60 after the second year. What does this total include?
options: Deposited money and interest earned over time.
Only the money paid into the account.
Only the interest earned in the second year.
Only payments made from the account.

This mistakes the final total for only the original deposit.
why.Only the interest earned in the second y: This leaves out the deposit and any earlier interest included in the total.
This confuses the final total with money paid out of the account.

activities.explanation: This is right because the total includes the deposit and the extra interest earned over time.

activities.prompt: A bank offers saving and borrowing. It also holds deposits and makes loans. Why can it offer these services?
options: It keeps deposits safe and lends them to others.
It uses deposits but ignores their safety.
It lends money without holding any deposits.
It keeps deposits safe but never lends them.

why.It uses deposits but ignores their safet: This wrongly assumes that using deposits means ignoring depositors' safety.
why.It lends money without holding any depos: This confuses lending money with having no deposits to lend.
why.It keeps deposits safe but never lends t: This wrongly assumes that banks never lend the money they hold.

activities.explanation: This is right because banks keep deposits safe and lend them to businesses or people.

lessons.title: Loans, Banking Access and the RBI

activities.prompt: How do banks turn savings into helpful loans—and who makes sure it works?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: Understanding Loans and Banking
activities.body: Banks lend money to people and businesses. People use loans for houses, vehicles and education. Businesses use them for machinery, materials, transport and products. Banks charge interest. Borrowers repay the amount and interest after the given period. The Reserve Bank of India supervises Indian banks. Jan Dhan Yojana and post offices also help people reach banking services.
keyPoints: People borrow for houses, vehicles and education.
Businesses borrow for machinery, materials, transport and products.
Borrowers repay the amount and interest after the given period.
The RBI is India's central bank and banker to banks.
activities.explanation: Loans help people and businesses, while banks and the RBI support the banking system.

activities.prompt: A family wants to buy a house but does not have enough money now. Should it take a bank loan?
steps: A bank lends money for buying a house, so a loan fits the family's need.
The bank charges interest, so the loan will cost the family money.
After the given period, the family must repay the loan amount and the interest.
Therefore, the family should borrow only if it can repay that total.
activities.explanation: Think it through with Hooty.

activities.prompt: Which is a use for a bank's loan to a person?
options: A house, vehicle or education
Machinery, raw materials or transport
Reserve money or bank supervision
Jan Dhan access or post offices
activities.explanation: Banks lend money for buying a house, vehicle or education.

activities.prompt: Banks charge interest from borrowers on the loans they provide.
activities.explanation: Interest is charged on bank loans. Borrowers repay it with the loan amount.

activities.prompt: Match each banking term to its correct detail.
activities.explanation: Jan Dhan Yojana began in 2014. The RBI is India's central bank, while post offices offer savings schemes.

activities.prompt: Banks charge ______ from borrowers on the loans they provide.
activities.hint: This is an amount paid for borrowing money.
activities.explanation: Banks charge interest on loans. This is part of what the borrower repays.

activities.prompt: Which statement describes a Jan Dhan bank account?
options: No minimum balance or fees
Minimum balance with yearly fees
Only business banking services
Only loans for transport
activities.explanation: Jan Dhan Yojana allowed accounts without a minimum balance or fees.

activities.prompt: Put the loan repayment steps in order.
items: The borrower repays the amount and interest
activities.explanation: The borrower pays back the loan amount and interest after the given period.

activities.prompt: Post offices supervise India's banking system.
activities.explanation: The Reserve Bank of India supervises Indian banks. Post offices provide financial services such as savings schemes.

activities.prompt: A bank keeps reserve money and lends some deposits. How does the bank earn income?
options: The difference between deposit and loan interest rates
The sum of deposit and loan interest rates
The amount kept as reserve money
The number of Jan Dhan accounts opened
activities.explanation: Banks earn the difference between deposit and loan interest rates. This difference gives them income.

activities.prompt: A report says more than 50 crore Jan Dhan accounts were opened. What can we safely say about the scheme?
options: It reached a very large number of people.
Only women were allowed to open accounts.
Every account in India came from this scheme.
Every business received a free loan.

why.Only women were allowed to open accounts: This is wrong because mainly women opened accounts, not only women.
why.Every account in India came from this sc: This is wrong because it wrongly assumes every Indian account came from the scheme.
This is wrong because the scheme gave bank access, not free business loans.

activities.explanation: This is right because more than 50 crore accounts show that many people used it.

activities.prompt: A bank keeps reserve money and lends other deposits. The loan interest rate is higher than the deposit rate. How does the bank earn income?
options: The difference between deposit and loan interest rates.
The money that banks keep as reserve money.
The number of bank accounts opened by women.
The central banking work done by the RBI.

why.The money that banks keep as reserve mon: This is wrong because reserve money is not the difference between interest rates.
why.The number of bank accounts opened by wo: This is wrong because account numbers do not create the bank's income.
why.The central banking work done by the RBI: This is wrong because the RBI's work is separate from the bank's income.

activities.explanation: This is right because the difference between the rates gives banks income.

lessons.title: Payment Modes and Systems

activities.prompt: How do different payment modes move money between people?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: Ways to Pay
activities.body: Payment modes are ways to pay. Common ones include cash, cheques and debit cards. A cheque is a paper instrument for paying someone directly from a bank account. Payment systems help move money from one person to another. UPI is a popular system for quick transfers. An ATM is a self-service cash machine available 24×7. Debit cards can also make shop payments.
keyPoints: Cash, cheques and debit cards are common payment modes.
Payment systems transfer money between people.
ATMs are self-service cash machines available 24×7.
activities.explanation: Great start! You now know several ways to pay and move money.

activities.prompt: A person wants to check account details, send money fast, and pay a shop. Which method fits each need?
steps: Internet banking fits checking because it shows balances and transaction history.
UPI fits sending because it transfers money quickly using a QR code.
A debit card fits the shop because it can make payments there.
So use internet banking, UPI, and a debit card for these needs.
activities.explanation: Think it through with Hooty.

activities.prompt: Which group lists common modes of payment?
options: Money, cheques and debit cards
Cash, cheques and debit cards
Cash, books and debit cards
Cash, cheques and credit cards
activities.explanation: Well done! Cash, cheques and debit cards are common payment modes.

activities.prompt: A cheque is a paper instrument for paying someone directly from a ______ account.
activities.hint: You keep your money in this kind of account.
activities.explanation: Good try! A cheque pays someone directly from a bank account.

activities.prompt: Match each payment method with its correct use.
pairs: Pay directly from a bank account
Transfer money quickly using a QR code
activities.explanation: Excellent matching! Each method has a special use.

activities.prompt: Put the cheque money-transfer steps in order.
activities.explanation: Nice work! The money moves from the issuer’s account to Rohan’s account.

activities.prompt: You want cash from an ATM at night. Which option is correct?
options: An ATM is self-service and available 24×7.
An ATM needs a staff member at night.
An ATM works only during bank hours.
An ATM can only show your balance.
activities.explanation: Right! ATMs are self-service machines available 24×7.

activities.prompt: UPI can transfer money quickly using a ______ code.
activities.hint: It is a type of code used for quick UPI transfers.
activities.explanation: Perfect! A QR code helps UPI transfer money quickly.

activities.prompt: ATMs are available 24×7. A person needs cash when the counter cannot help. Which method works at any time?
options: Use a debit card, because ATMs give cash at any time.
Use a withdrawal slip, because the cash counter gives cash.
Use a cheque, because it can be used at an ATM.
Use UPI, because it gives cash from an ATM.

why.Use a withdrawal slip, because the cash: This mistake thinks a withdrawal slip works without the cash counter.
why.Use a cheque, because it can be used at: This mistake thinks a cheque is a card for using an ATM.
why.Use UPI, because it gives cash from an A: This mistake thinks UPI is a way to withdraw cash.

activities.explanation: This is right because a debit card works at an always-available ATM.

activities.prompt: Debit cards can make shop payments. A bank customer needs cash from a counter. Which pair fits both needs?
options: Cash for the shop; debit card for the bank.
Debit card for the shop; withdrawal slip for the bank.
Cheque for the shop; UPI for the bank.
UPI for the shop; cheque for the bank.

why.Cash for the shop; debit card for the ba: This mistake swaps the shop and bank payment methods.
This mistake treats a cheque and UPI as cash withdrawal methods.
This mistake thinks UPI and cheques are the best counter methods.

activities.explanation: This is right because cards pay at shops and slips are used at the counter.

activities.prompt: Debit cards can pay at shops. A shopper has a card and a withdrawal slip. Which item should be used, and why?
options: The withdrawal slip, because it can make payments at shops.
The debit card, because it can make payments at shops.
The debit card, because it withdraws cash at the counter.
The withdrawal slip, because it checks the balance.

why.The withdrawal slip, because it can make: This mistake thinks a withdrawal slip is used to pay a shop.
why.The debit card, because it withdraws cas: This mistake thinks withdrawing cash also makes a shop payment.
why.The withdrawal slip, because it checks t: This mistake thinks a withdrawal slip shows account details.

activities.explanation: This is right because debit cards can make payments at shops.

activities.prompt: Internet banking shows balances and transaction history. UPI can send money quickly. Which method fits both account needs?
options: A debit card, because it shows both account details.
A cheque, because it checks details before sending money.
Internet banking, because it can do both jobs.
Cash, because it shows every past transaction.

why.A debit card, because it shows both acco: This mistake thinks a debit card shows balances and history.
why.A cheque, because it checks details befo: This mistake thinks a cheque checks online account details.
why.Cash, because it shows every past transa: This mistake thinks cash can display past transactions.

activities.explanation: This is right because internet banking checks details and transfers money.

lessons.title: Stock Market and Shares

activities.prompt: How do people buy, sell, and own pieces of companies?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: Understanding Shares
activities.body: The stock market is where people buy and sell shares. A share gives part-ownership in a company. Companies issue shares to raise money for their operations. Trading happens at a stock exchange. The Bombay Stock Exchange was established in 1875. Share prices can rise or fall, so people may make gains or losses. A fall in many share prices can result in a stock market crash.
keyPoints: A share gives part-ownership in a company.
Companies issue shares to raise money.
Trading shares happens at a stock exchange.
Changing share prices can bring gains or losses.
activities.explanation: Good start! Shares help companies raise money while giving owners part-ownership.

activities.prompt: A company needs money for its operations. Two people buy newly issued shares, and one buys more. What happens?
steps: The company issues shares because this raises money for its operations.
Both buyers become part-owners because each share is part-ownership.
The larger buyer has higher ownership because more shares mean more ownership.
Therefore, the company raises money, and the larger buyer owns a bigger part.
activities.explanation: Think it through with Hooty.

activities.prompt: What is a share?
options: Part-ownership in a company
A place for buying shares
A company worker's salary
A type of market stall
activities.explanation: A share gives its owner part-ownership in a company.

activities.prompt: A collection of shares is called a stock.
activities.explanation: Yes! A collection of shares is called a stock.

activities.prompt: Match each phrase with its meaning.
activities.explanation: You matched each phrase with the correct idea from the lesson.

activities.prompt: What happens when a company has problems?
options: Share prices rise quickly
Share prices drop
Share prices stay steady
Share prices rise slightly
activities.explanation: Fewer people want the shares, so their price drops.

activities.prompt: The Bombay Stock Exchange was established in ______.
activities.hint: Think about the year given in the lesson.
activities.explanation: The Bombay Stock Exchange was established in 1875.

activities.prompt: Your share prices fall. What may happen to your money?
options: You may have a loss
You may have a gain
You will have no change
You will always have a gain
activities.explanation: Falling prices can cause losses because share prices fluctuate.

activities.prompt: Two children own the same company's shares. One owns more shares than the other. Who has higher ownership?
options: The child with more shares, because more shares mean higher ownership.
The child with fewer shares, because fewer shares mean higher ownership.
Both have equal ownership, because each child owns at least one share.
Neither child, because shares do not give part-ownership in companies.

why.The child with fewer shares, because few: This reverses the rule that more shares mean higher ownership.
why.Both have equal ownership, because each: This wrongly treats one share and many shares as equal ownership.
why.Neither child, because shares do not giv: This denies that a share is part-ownership in a company.

activities.explanation: More shares mean a larger part-ownership in the company.

activities.prompt: A company has problems. People want fewer of its shares. What will likely happen to the share price?
options: The price will drop, because fewer people want the company's shares.
The price will rise, because fewer people want the company's shares.
The price will drop, because more people want the company's shares.
The price will stay, because fewer people want the company's shares.

why.The price will rise, because fewer peopl: This wrongly connects fewer buyers with a rising share price.
why.The price will drop, because more people: This gives the wrong reason for a falling share price.
why.The price will stay, because fewer peopl: This wrongly treats lower demand as having no effect on price.

activities.explanation: Fewer people wanting shares makes their price fall.

activities.prompt: Share prices fall across many companies. What can this cause, according to the lesson?
options: A stock market crash, because many falling prices can cause one.
A stock market boom, because many falling prices can cause one.
A stock market crash, because one falling price can cause one.
A stock market crash, because every small fall can cause one.

why.A stock market boom, because many fallin: This confuses falling prices with a rising stock market.
why.A stock market crash, because one fallin: It leaves out the many falling prices needed for a crash.
why.A stock market crash, because every smal: It wrongly assumes every small fall causes a crash.

activities.explanation: A fall in many share prices can result in a stock market crash.

activities.prompt: A buyer hopes a stock's value will rise. It rises, and the buyer sells. What likely happened?
options: The buyer made a gain, because the selling price was higher.
The buyer made a loss, because the selling price was higher.
The buyer made no gain or loss, because the selling price was higher.
The buyer made a gain, because share prices never fluctuate.

why.The buyer made a loss, because the selli: This wrongly connects a higher selling price with a loss.
why.The buyer made no gain or loss, because: It wrongly ignores the rise between buying and selling.
why.The buyer made a gain, because share pri: It wrongly treats changing prices as if they never happened.

activities.explanation: Selling at a higher price than the buying price brings a gain.

lessons.title: Digital Safety and Financial Infrastructure

activities.prompt: How can you stay safe when paying digitally?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: Stay Safe and Know Why Money Systems Matter
activities.body: Digital payments make life easier, but you must beware of fraud and scams. Fraudsters may use fake calls or messages. They can trick you into downloading harmful apps or sharing bank details and OTPs. OTPs are details you must never share with strangers. Avoid unknown message links, and report fraud through helpline 1930. Financial infrastructure helps people save, borrow and invest. These boost economic activity and contribute to national prosperity.
keyPoints: Digital payment users must beware of fraud and scams.
Protect account details, passwords and OTPs from strangers.
Financial infrastructure supports savings, credit and investment.
activities.explanation: Staying alert helps you enjoy digital payments safely.

activities.prompt: What should you do if a message asks for your OTP?
steps: Fake messages may ask for harmful app downloads, so be careful.
Do not share bank details or OTPs with strangers, because fraudsters misuse them.
Avoid unknown links, because they may lead to fraud.
Report fraud through 1930 or the portal, so it can be checked.
activities.explanation: Think it through with Hooty.

activities.title: Choose Safely
activities.prompt: Which action helps protect you from digital fraud?
options: Avoid unknown message links
Click every message link
Share your account number
Download every new app
activities.explanation: Unknown links can lead to harmful apps. Avoiding them keeps you safer.

activities.title: True or False?
activities.prompt: Fraudsters may use fake calls or messages.
activities.explanation: Fake calls and messages are ways fraudsters trick people.

activities.title: Complete the Rule
activities.prompt: Avoid clicking unknown ______ or videos received through messages.
activities.hint: These can be sent to you in a message.
activities.explanation: Unknown links may lead to harmful apps, so leave them alone.

activities.title: Protect Your Details
activities.prompt: A stranger asks for your OTP. What should you do?
options: Never share it
Share it quickly
Read it aloud
Send it by message
activities.explanation: Fraudsters may trick people into sharing OTPs. Never share them with strangers.

activities.title: Match Each Warning
activities.prompt: Match each warning with its safe action.
pairs: Do not store it on devices
activities.explanation: Each pair follows a safety rule that helps protect you from fraud.

activities.title: True or False?
activities.prompt: Financial infrastructure supports only digital payments.
activities.explanation: It also promotes savings, credit and investment. These boost economic activity.

activities.title: Trace the Fraud Chain
activities.prompt: Put the fraud chain in the correct order.
items: Fraudsters use fake calls or messages
They trick people into sharing bank details or OTPs
They gain access to a mobile or computer
They steal personal data or drain bank money
activities.explanation: Fake messages can begin the chain. Shared details can then give fraudsters access and cause harm.

activities.title: Why It Matters
activities.prompt: Why does financial infrastructure matter to the nation?
options: It boosts economic activity and national prosperity
It speeds up every message and call
It removes money from every bank account
It replaces all savings, credit and investment
activities.explanation: It promotes savings, credit and investment. These boost economic activity and contribute to national prosperity.

activities.prompt: A fake message asks for an app download. Why might this harm you?
options: The app may make digital payments easier for everyone.
Fraudsters may steal data and drain money.
Your bank may send more useful payment messages.
The message may help your family save money.

why.The app may make digital payments easier: This ignores the warning about harmful apps.
why.Your bank may send more useful payment m: This mistakes a fake message for a useful bank message.
why.The message may help your family save mo: This focuses on saving instead of digital safety.

activities.explanation: Fake apps can lead to stolen data and lost money.

activities.prompt: A fraudster asks for your OTP. Why might your device become unsafe?
options: They may make your payments easier to complete.
They may become a friend who helps you.
They may stop fake messages from reaching you.
They may gain access and steal personal data.

why.They may make your payments easier to co: This mistakes fraud for a helpful payment service.
Fraudsters are not trying to be genuine friends.
why.They may stop fake messages from reachin: This wrongly treats a request for an OTP as protection.

activities.explanation: Sharing an OTP can help fraudsters access your device and data.

activities.context: Navdeep deposits his surplus money with a bank. Rima needs money for her bamboo business. The bank provides Rima with the remaining amount she needs as a loan. A bank collects money from people as deposits and lends money to borrowers for specific purposes. Banks, payment systems and stock markets are part of financial infrastructure, which helps people, businesses and the government manage money and make financial transactions.
activities.prompt: If the bank lends Rima only part of the amount she still needs, what is the most likely result?
options: Some of the money needed for her bamboo business would still be missing.
All of the money needed for her bamboo business would be available.
Her bamboo business would need twice as much money.
No money would be lent to her bamboo business.

why.All of the money needed for her bamboo b: Incorrect: a partial loan cannot cover the full need.
why.Her bamboo business would need twice as: Incorrect: a partial loan does not double the need.
why.No money would be lent to her bamboo bus: Incorrect: the bank still makes some loan, so it does not lend nothing.

activities.explanation: Correct: a partial loan reduces, but does not remove, Rima's money need.

activities.context: Navdeep deposits his surplus money with a bank. Rima needs money for her bamboo business. The bank provides Rima with the remaining amount she needs as a loan. A bank collects money from people as deposits and lends money to borrowers for specific purposes. Banks, payment systems and stock markets are part of financial infrastructure, which helps people, businesses and the government manage money and make financial transactions.
activities.prompt: Why is the bank's lending activity important for infrastructure development and maintenance?
options: It can provide funding for infrastructure development and maintenance.
It allows the bank to build roads and railways directly.
It means financial transactions will no longer be possible.
It removes the government's need to manage money.

why.It allows the bank to build roads and ra: Incorrect: a bank provides money rather than building physical infrastructure.
why.It means financial transactions will no: Incorrect: financial infrastructure supports financial transactions.
why.It removes the government's need to mana: Incorrect: the government still uses financial infrastructure to manage money.

activities.explanation: Correct: lending makes funding for development and maintenance possible.

activities.prompt: Explain the difference between physical infrastructure and financial infrastructure.
activities.answer: Physical infrastructure includes roads, railways and telecommunication. Financial infrastructure includes banks, payment systems and stock markets. Their difference is that physical infrastructure consists of physical examples, while financial infrastructure is a network that helps people, businesses and the government manage money and make financial transactions.
points: Identifies roads, railways and telecommunication as physical infrastructure.
Identifies banks, payment systems and stock markets as financial infrastructure.
Explains the money-management and transaction role of financial infrastructure.
activities.explanation: Compare your answer with the points a marker looks for.

activities.context: A shopkeeper opens a current account to make and receive payments, while a nurse opens a savings account. Banks keep deposits safe and lend them to businesses or other people. Depositors receive extra money over a regular period as interest. When interest is earned on earlier interest, the balance grows through compounding. The nurse's passbook records all receipts and payments. In the example, the total after the second year is ₹1,123.60.
activities.prompt: After the first year's interest is added to the nurse's balance, what happens next if that interest also earns interest?
options: The balance grows again because new interest is calculated using the earlier interest too.
The balance stays unchanged because new interest is calculated only on the original deposit.
The balance falls because the earlier interest is deducted before the next interest is added.
The balance grows only once because new interest cannot be added to earlier interest.

why.The balance stays unchanged because new: Only the original deposit earning interest stops compounding.
why.The balance falls because the earlier in: Interest is added; it is not deducted from the balance.
why.The balance grows only once because new: The earlier interest can earn further interest.

activities.explanation: This is compounding: new interest uses the earlier interest.

activities.context: A shopkeeper opens a current account to make and receive payments, while a nurse opens a savings account. Banks keep deposits safe and lend them to businesses or other people. Depositors receive extra money over a regular period as interest. When interest is earned on earlier interest, the balance grows through compounding. The nurse's passbook records all receipts and payments. In the example, the total after the second year is ₹1,123.60.
activities.prompt: If the shopkeeper wants an account that will keep money for a fixed period, which account should she open?
options: She should open a fixed deposit account because it keeps money for a fixed period.
She should open a savings account because it is mainly intended for individuals.
She should open a current account because it helps businesses make and receive payments.
She should keep using a current account because every account keeps money for a fixed period.

why.She should open a savings account becaus: A savings account is mainly for individuals.
why.She should open a current account becaus: A current account is intended for business and trading payments.
why.She should keep using a current account: Current accounts do not have the fixed-period purpose described.

activities.explanation: A fixed deposit account is intended to keep money for a fixed period.

activities.prompt: Explain why a person or business must open a bank account before using bank services.
activities.answer: A person or business must first open a bank account to use bank services. These services include saving, withdrawing and borrowing. The account holder can then use the bank to keep money safe, receive or make payments, and access interest through an appropriate account.
points: An account must be opened first.
Bank services include saving, withdrawing and borrowing.
The account holder can then use the services.
Interest may be received over a regular period.
activities.explanation: Compare your answer with the points a marker looks for.

activities.prompt: Explain why banks charge interest on loans and how this helps them earn income.
activities.answer: Banks charge interest because they lend money to borrowers. After the given period, borrowers repay the loan amount along with the interest. When the interest received on loans is higher than the interest paid on deposits, the difference between the two rates becomes income for the bank.
points: Banks lend money to borrowers.
Borrowers repay the loan amount and interest after the given period.
Banks receive interest on the loans they provide.
The difference between deposit and loan interest rates gives banks income.
activities.explanation: Compare your answer with the points a marker looks for.

activities.prompt: Explain the difference between a debit card and UPI.
activities.answer: A debit card can make payments at shops and withdraw cash from ATMs. UPI is electronic and can transfer money quickly between accounts using a QR code. The main difference is that a debit card directly supports shop payments and cash withdrawals, while UPI supports account-to-account transfers.
points: Debit cards can be used to make payments at shops.
Debit cards can withdraw cash from ATMs.
UPI can transfer money quickly using a QR code.
Electronic payment methods allow instant transfers between accounts.
activities.explanation: Compare your answer with the points a marker looks for.

activities.context: At a stock exchange, a person buys some shares in a company to become part-owner and help the company raise money for its operations. The person hopes the value of these shares will rise. Later, the company faces problems. Fewer people want to buy its shares, so their price drops. The person worries because trading shares can bring gains or losses.
activities.prompt: If the company's share price falls, what happens to the person's ownership?
options: It stays at the same level because the number of shares owned has not changed.
It falls because each share is now worth less.
It rises because each share is now worth less.
It becomes zero because the company has problems.

why.It falls because each share is now worth: Incorrect: a lower price does not reduce the number owned.
why.It rises because each share is now worth: Incorrect: a lower price does not increase ownership.
why.It becomes zero because the company has: Incorrect: problems and a price fall do not remove ownership.

activities.explanation: Correct: ownership depends on the number of shares owned.

activities.context: At a stock exchange, a person buys some shares in a company to become part-owner and help the company raise money for its operations. The person hopes the value of these shares will rise. Later, the company faces problems. Fewer people want to buy its shares, so their price drops. The person worries because trading shares can bring gains or losses.
activities.prompt: What can a fall in many share prices result in?
options: A stock market crash.
A larger collection of shares for each owner.
Higher ownership in every company.
A reduction in companies' need for money.

why.A larger collection of shares for each o: Incorrect: a crash does not give owners more shares.
Incorrect: share prices and ownership are different.
why.A reduction in companies' need for money: Incorrect: companies still issue shares to raise money for operations.

activities.explanation: Correct: a fall in many prices can cause a crash.

activities.prompt: What is the difference between a share and a stock?
activities.answer: A share is one part-ownership in a company. A stock is a collection of shares. Therefore, owning a share means holding part-ownership in a company, while owning a stock means holding a collection of shares.
points: A share represents part-ownership.
A stock is a collection of shares.
The terms describe different sizes of shareholding.
activities.explanation: Compare your answer with the points a marker looks for.

activities.context: A student receives a fake call from a fraudster offering help with digital payments. The student downloads a harmful app and shares bank details and a One-Time Password. The fraudster gains access to the student’s mobile, steals personal data from the device, and drains money from the bank account. The student should avoid unknown links or videos, should not store sensitive banking information on the device, and report the fraud through helpline 1930 or the National Cybercrime Reporting Portal.
activities.prompt: What should the student do after noticing that money and personal data have been taken?
options: Call 1930 or use the national cybercrime portal.
Ask the caller to prove their identity and continue the conversation.
Click a message link to look for the missing money.
Store the banking details on the phone for later.

why.Ask the caller to prove their identity a: Strangers should not be trusted with account information.
why.Click a message link to look for the mis: Unknown message links should be avoided.
why.Store the banking details on the phone f: Sensitive banking information should not be stored on devices.

activities.explanation: This is the correct way to report fraud.

activities.context: A student receives a fake call from a fraudster offering help with digital payments. The student downloads a harmful app and shares bank details and a One-Time Password. The fraudster gains access to the student’s mobile, steals personal data from the device, and drains money from the bank account. The student should avoid unknown links or videos, should not store sensitive banking information on the device, and report the fraud through helpline 1930 or the National Cybercrime Reporting Portal.
activities.prompt: If the student had refused the caller’s request, which action would have protected the device and account?
options: Avoid unknown links and refuse to share the One-Time Password.
Share the bank details but keep the One-Time Password secret.
Download the app to inspect it and then decide whether to use it.
Save the One-Time Password on the phone for the next payment.

why.Share the bank details but keep the One-: Bank details should also be kept private.
why.Download the app to inspect it and then: Downloading a harmful app can expose the device.
why.Save the One-Time Password on the phone: Sensitive banking information should not be saved on devices.

activities.explanation: Unknown links and shared OTPs create safety risks.

activities.prompt: Explain the difference between the convenience of digital payments and the broader role of financial infrastructure.
activities.answer: Digital payments make everyday tasks easier, but users must beware of fraud and scams. Financial infrastructure has a wider economic role: it promotes savings, credit and investment. These activities boost economic activity, which ultimately contributes to the nation’s prosperity.
points: Digital payments make life easier.
Users must still beware of fraud and scams.
Financial infrastructure promotes savings, credit and investment.
This activity contributes to national prosperity.
activities.explanation: Compare your answer with the points a marker looks for.
